# Animation

256 tools. Back to the [index](README.md).

## `add_anim_bone_track`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Add the animation track of one skeleton bone to a UAnimSequence through its data controller, filled with num_keys identity keys (zero translation, identity rotation, unit scale), as one undo step, then save the package. An existing track stays but its keys are replaced (idempotent); when that leaves the stored track data as it was (measured with the data model GUID; the engine stores a constant track as one value, whatever num_keys is) the reply is a success with changed=false and saved=false, the package keeps the dirty state it had and nothing is saved. A bone_name the sequence's skeleton does not have is an error and nothing is written; an omitted bone_name targets the root bone. A missing sequence or skeleton is an error and a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Real poses: set_anim_bone_track_keys; inverse: remove_anim_bone_track.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `bone_name` | string | no | Name of a bone of the skeleton of the sequence; omitted or empty means the root bone. |
| `num_keys` | number | no | Number of identity keys to write, rounded, minimum 1 (default 2); not checked against the frame count of the sequence. |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, bone_name, num_bone_tracks, num_keys, changed, success, saved, save_error, message }`

## `add_anim_composite_segment`

*Additive.*

Append an FAnimSegment referencing a real UAnimSequence to a UAnimComposite's AnimationTrack, then recompute its length. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `composite_path` | string | yes | Object path of the UAnimComposite (e.g. "/Game/Animation/AC_Example"). |
| `animation_path` | string | yes | Object path of the UAnimSequence to reference. |
| `start_pos` | number | no | Segment start position; ignored after auto-stacking (default 0) |
| `play_rate` | number | no | Segment play rate (default 1.0) |
| `loop_count` | number | no | Segment loop count, minimum 1 (default 1) |

**Returns:** `{ composite_path, animation_path, num_segments, composite_length, segments, success, saved, save_error }`

## `add_anim_conduit`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add a conduit node named conduit_name to an existing state machine of an Animation Blueprint (a missing blueprint or machine is an error; create the machine with add_anim_state_machine), then mark the blueprint structurally modified and save it without compiling. Idempotent by name: an existing conduit is returned unchanged (already_existed true). The conduit is placed unconnected: link it to states with add_anim_transition; remove_anim_conduit undoes it. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error, the change kept in memory.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Path to the UAnimBlueprint asset |
| `machine_name` | string | yes | Name of the target state machine |
| `conduit_name` | string | yes | Name for the new conduit |

**Returns:** `{ anim_blueprint_path: string, machine_name: string, conduit_name: string, node_class: string, conduit_created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, conduit_count: int, save_error?: string }`

## `add_anim_curve_name`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Register a curve name as curve metadata on a USkeleton (USkeleton::AddCurveMetaData) in an undo transaction, then save the skeleton package. Idempotent: a name already registered is a success with added=false, already_existed=true and saved=false, and the skeleton is neither modified nor saved. It adds no keys -- to put a keyed float curve on a UAnimSequence use add_anim_float_curve; remove_anim_curve_name is the inverse. An unknown skeleton is an error and a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `curve_name` | string | yes | The curve name to add (e.g. 'Curve_Example'). |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Asset path of the USkeleton to edit (/Game/...); when omitted or empty the engine asset /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton is edited and saved. |

**Returns:** `{ skeleton_path, curve_name, present, added, already_existed, curve_count, saved, save_error, message }`

## `add_anim_float_curve`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Add a float curve (Editable flag) to a UAnimSequence through its data controller and set its keys from [time, value] pairs as linear keys with auto tangents, in one undo step, then save the package. An existing float curve of that name is kept and its keys are replaced (idempotent); one that already holds exactly those keys is a success with changed=false and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved. curve_found confirms the curve and num_keys counts the keys sent. A missing sequence is an error and a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Rekey: set_anim_curve_keys; transform curves: add_anim_transform_curve; a skeleton-only name: add_anim_curve_name; read back: get_anim_curve_data.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `curve_name` | string | yes | Float curve name to add. |
| `keys` | array | no | JSON array of [time, value] pairs (default [[0,0],[1,1]]) |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, curve_name, num_float_curves, num_keys, curve_found, changed, success, saved, save_error, message }`

## `add_anim_notify`

*Additive.*

Add an instance of a UAnimNotify class at a time on a UAnimSequence notify track (created when missing) and save the sequence; each call adds another event, and an unknown class is an error. Returns time and success. For montages use add_montage_notify; for durations add_anim_notify_state. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `animation_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UAnimSequence. |
| `notify_name` | string | yes | Class name of a loaded UAnimNotify subclass, tried as given and then with the AnimNotify_ prefix (e.g. 'AN_Footstep', or "PlaySound" for AnimNotify_PlaySound); a Blueprint notify goes by its generated name ending in _C. |
| `time` | number | no | Notify trigger time in seconds (default 0) |
| `track_name` | string | no | Notify track name (default 'Default') |

**Returns:** `{ animation_path, notify_name, time, success, saved, save_error, message }`

## `add_anim_state_machine`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add a state machine node named machine_name to the top-level AnimGraph of an Animation Blueprint, then mark the blueprint structurally modified and save it without compiling (compile_anim_blueprint gives runtime effect). Idempotent by name: an existing machine is returned unchanged (already_existed true). The node starts with only its entry and is not connected to the Output Pose: wire it with connect_anim_graph_pins, fill it with add_anim_state, add_anim_conduit and add_anim_transition, or build it in one call with build_animation_state_machine. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error, the change kept in memory.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Path to the UAnimBlueprint asset |
| `machine_name` | string | yes | Name for the new state machine |

**Returns:** `{ anim_blueprint_path: string, machine_name: string, node_class: string, state_machine_graph: string, state_machine_created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, state_machine_count: int, save_error?: string }`

## `add_anim_transform_curve`

*Destructive.*

Add a transform curve (RCT_Transform) to a UAnimSequence via the data controller and set its keys as linear keys per axis, in one undo step, then save the package; the sampling rate of the sequence is left as it is. An existing transform curve of that name is kept and its keys are replaced; one that already holds exactly those keys is a success with changed=false, keys_set=false and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Object path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `curve_name` | string | yes | Name of the transform curve to add. |
| `keys` | array | no | JSON array of {time, location:[x,y,z], rotation:[pitch,yaw,roll], scale:[x,y,z]} objects |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, curve_name, num_transform_curves, num_keys, keys_set, changed, success, saved, save_error, message? }`

## `add_bone`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add a bone named bone_name to the reference skeleton of a USkeleton asset under parent_name (omitted or empty: an extra root bone), with local_transform relative to the parent (a zero or missing scale becomes 1), then save the skeleton. Idempotent by name: an existing bone is returned (added false, already_existed true) without checking its parent or saving. An unknown parent is an error, and so is a failed save. Only the skeleton changes: skeletal meshes using it get no new bone, and there is no undo entry. No commit_bone_changes is needed; set_bone_parent and set_bone_transform edit bones, add_virtual_bone adds virtual ones.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | Path to the USkeleton asset |
| `bone_name` | string | yes | Name for the new bone; when a bone of that name already exists nothing changes (added false) |
| `parent_name` | string | no | Parent bone name, or empty/null for a new root bone |
| `local_transform` | object | no | Optional {location:[x,y,z], rotation:[p,y,r], scale:[x,y,z]}, defaults to identity |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, bone_name, bone_index, parent_index, bone_count, added, already_existed, saved, op: "add_bone" }`

## `add_ik_goal`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add an IK goal to an IK Rig, associated with a bone, through the IK Rig controller (one undo transaction), then save the asset.  If bone_name is omitted, a leaf bone of the rig's skeletal mesh is picked automatically. Idempotent: a goal of that name on the same bone is not re-created but returned with already_exists=true, saved=false and a note, and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset |
| `goal_name` | string | yes | Unique name for the new goal |
| `bone_name` | string | no | Optional bone name to attach the goal to |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, goal_name: string, bone_name: string, goal_count: int, saved: bool, already_exists?: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `add_ik_retarget_chain`

*Additive.*

Add a retarget bone chain from start_bone to end_bone, optionally tied to an IK goal, to an IK Rig asset and save it. Both bones must exist in the skeleton of the rig; the chain name is made unique, so read chain_name back. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | IK Rig (UIKRigDefinition) asset path, e.g. "/Game/Retarget/IK_Hero". |
| `chain_name` | string | yes | Name for the new retarget chain (uniquified by the engine) |
| `start_bone` | string | yes | First bone of the chain; must exist in the skeleton of the rig. |
| `end_bone` | string | yes | Last bone of the chain; must exist in the skeleton of the rig. |
| `goal_name` | string | no | IK goal to attach the chain to (default none); not checked against the goals of the rig. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, chain_name: string, start_bone: string, end_bone: string, goal_name: string, chain_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_motion_warping_component`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Attach a UMotionWarpingComponent to an actor in the editor world. Idempotent: if the actor already has one, returns the existing instance with already_existed:true instead of creating a duplicate. The component is NewObject&lt;UMotionWarpingComponent>(Actor, FName("MotionWarping")) followed by RegisterComponent() so it shows up in GetComponents() immediately. The owning world's level is marked dirty so the editor persists the change on save; no explicit SavePackage call (avoids the noise of saving a transient actor out of an editor world).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_path` | string | yes | Full editor path (e.g. "/Game/Maps/Test.Test:PersistentLevel.ActorName") or short name of the actor. |

**Returns:** `{ actor_path: string, component_path: string, already_existed: bool }`

## `add_pose_to_pose_asset`

*Destructive.*

Add a pose copied from the skeleton reference pose to a UPoseAsset under the given name (a pose of that name is replaced) in an undo transaction and save it; refused when the asset has no skeleton. A pose of that name that already holds exactly that reference pose (every bone a track, zero curve values, no source animation GUID) is a success with added=false, already_existed=true and saved=false, and the asset is neither modified nor saved. Returns num_poses, num_tracks and already_existed. For poses from animation frames use create_pose_asset_from_anim_sequence. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pose_asset_path` | string | yes | Path to the UPoseAsset (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/Pose_Example'). |
| `pose_name` | string | yes | Name of the pose to add (e.g. 'RefPose_A'). |

**Returns:** `{ pose_asset_path, pose_name, num_poses, num_tracks, present, added, already_existed, saved, save_error, message }`

*Additive.*

Add a retarget op to the op stack of an IK Retargeter asset through its controller (one undo transaction), then save the asset; op_index and op_name are where and how the engine placed it. Default type: FK Chains op. An unknown op type, or a singleton op type the stack already has, is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| `ik_retargeter_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRetargeter asset |
| `op_type` | string | no | Optional op class path (default "/Script/IKRig.IKRetargetFKChainsOp") |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, op_index: int, op_name: string, op_type: string, op_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_rigvm_link`

*Destructive.*

Link an output pin to an input pin in the main RigVM graph of a Control Rig Blueprint (URigVMController::AddLink with its undo, as the editor links, so a new link is one undo step); a link already into that input pin, into a pin inside it or into the pin it is part of, or out of an execute output pin, is replaced. Pins are NodeName.PinName paths as get_rigvm_graph lists them. A new link is then compiled and saved; a failed link (pins missing, incompatible or already linked) is an error with linked and saved false, the graph is left as it was (links the attempt broke are restored) and nothing is compiled or saved. Refused during PIE unless force. Add nodes with add_rigvm_node and set unlinked inputs with set_rigvm_pin_default; Blueprint graphs use connect_pins.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UControlRigBlueprint asset |
| `source_pin` | string | yes | Output pin path NodeA.PinName |
| `target_pin` | string | yes | Input pin path NodeB.PinName |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, source_pin: string, target_pin: string, linked: bool, link_count: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }`

Add a rig-unit node to a Control Rig's RigVM solver graph

| `node_type` | string | yes | BeginExecution, PrepareForExecution, GetTransform, SetTransform, AimBone, or TwoBoneIKSimple |

*Additive.*

Append a new LOD entry to a skeletal mesh (clone of LOD 0 build settings).

| `screen_size` | number | no | Optional override for ScreenSize.Default of the new LOD (default 0.5) |

## `add_skeletal_mesh_socket`

*Additive.*

Add a socket on a named bone of a skeletal mesh asset (undoable) and save the mesh. A copy also goes to the mesh's skeleton, which is then saved too; when the skeleton already has a socket of that name, the mesh has no skeleton, or the skeleton is engine content or under a read-only root, no copy is made (added_to_skeleton false) and skeleton_note says why. Errors, writing nothing, when the mesh does not load, the mesh already has a socket of that name, or the bone is missing from the mesh or its skeleton. success is false when a changed package fails to save. Edit existing sockets with set_skeletal_mesh_socket_transform or rename_skeletal_mesh_socket; skeleton-only sockets with add_socket_to_skeleton_asset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset |
| `socket_name` | string | yes | Name for the new socket; leading and trailing spaces are trimmed, and a name the mesh already has is an error. |
| `bone_name` | string | yes | Name of the bone to attach the socket to; it must exist in the mesh and, when the copy goes to the skeleton, in the skeleton too. |
| `location` | array | no | Optional [x, y, z] relative location |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] relative rotation |

**Returns:** `{ socket_name: string, bone_name: string, socket_count: int, location_x: float, location_y: float, location_z: float, added_to_skeleton: bool, skeleton_path: string, skeleton_note: string?, saved: bool, save_error: string?, skeleton_saved: bool?, skeleton_save_error: string? }`

## `add_socket_to_skeleton_asset`

*Additive.*

Add a socket to a USkeleton asset on a bone (the root by default) at a bone-relative location and rotation, then save; an existing socket of that name is updated in place (already_existed true). A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. A socket on a skeletal mesh asset (copied to its skeleton when that skeleton is project content): add_skeletal_mesh_socket.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | USkeleton asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton". |
| `socket_name` | string | yes | Name of the socket; an existing socket with this name is updated instead of duplicated. |
| `bone_name` | string | no | Bone to attach the socket to; must exist in the skeleton (default the root bone). |
| `location` | array | no | Socket location relative to its bone as [x, y, z] (default 0,0,0) |
| `rotation` | array | no | Socket rotation relative to its bone as [pitch, yaw, roll] (default 0,0,0) |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, socket_name: string, bone_name: string, socket_count: int, added: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string? }`

## `add_virtual_bone`

*Additive.*

Add a virtual bone from a source bone to a target bone of a USkeleton asset, named "VB &lt;source>_&lt;target>" by the engine, then save. Bone names are not checked against the skeleton; an existing pair returns that bone with already_exists true. Returns virtual_bone_name and virtual_bone_count.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | USkeleton asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton". |
| `source_bone` | string | no | Bone the virtual bone starts from (default the first bone, usually the root); not validated. |
| `target_bone` | string | no | Bone the virtual bone points to (default the first bone that differs from source_bone); not validated. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, virtual_bone_name: string, source_bone: string, target_bone: string, virtual_bone_count: int, saved: bool, already_exists: bool }`

## `add_warp_target_to_component`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Add (or update in-place) a FMotionWarpingTarget on an existing UMotionWarpingComponent. Exactly one of three payload shapes must be supplied: (1) component_path -> AddOrUpdateWarpTargetFromComponent(name, comp, NAME_None, false, TargetsForwardVector, ZeroVector, ZeroRotator); (2) location + rotation -> AddOrUpdateWarpTargetFromLocationAndRotation; (3) location only -> AddOrUpdateWarpTargetFromLocation. The engine API is idempotent by WarpTargetName (replace-in-place). Marking the owning actor dirty so the editor persists the change.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_path` | string | yes | Full editor path or short name of the actor. |
| `target_name` | string | yes | FName identifier for the warp target. |
| `location` | array | no | Optional world [x, y, z] location for the target. |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional world [pitch, yaw, roll] rotation in degrees for the target. |
| `component_path` | string | no | Optional name of a USceneComponent on the actor to drive the target transform. |

**Returns:** `{ actor_path: string, target_name: string, warp_target_count: int, source: string, already_existed: bool }`

Assign a physics asset to a skeletal mesh (or pass null/empty to clear it).

**Returns:** `{ skeletal_mesh_path: string, old_lod_count: int, new_lod_count: int, lod_count: int, baked: bool, regenerate_even_if_imported: bool, generate_base_lod: bool, bake_warning: string }`

## `build_animation_state_machine`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Atomic JSON-spec builder for an Animation Blueprint state machine. Builds (or reuses) the state machine, then iterates states, transitions, and per-transition rules in one idempotent call. Replaces 8+ primitive cmds (add_anim_state_machine + add_anim_state + add_anim_transition + set_anim_transition_rule_*) with a single spec. Re-running with the same spec is a no-op (each primitive is internally idempotent: state-by-name, transition-by-source+target). For repeated invocations that change rule shape, the rule is re-applied on the existing transition.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Path to the UAnimBlueprint asset |
| `state_machine_name` | string | yes | Target state machine name (created if missing via add_anim_state_machine) |
| `spec` | object | yes | JSON describing the graph shape. states: [{name: str, animation?: str (/Game/Anim/Foo — optional; load-bearing for the runtime state asset but NOT created here), loop?: bool, pos?: [x, y]}]. transitions: [{from: str, to: str, blend?: number (= crossfade_duration seconds), bidirectional?: bool, priority_order?: int, rule?: object}]. Each rule variant maps 1:1 to an existing primitive cmd: {type: "automatic", enabled?: bool = false, trigger_time?: number = 0.0} \| {type: "bool", variable: str (must exist on the AnimBP), invert?: bool = false} \| {type: "comparison", variable: str (must be float/double on the AnimBP), operator: "=="\|"!="\|">"\|"&lt;"\|">="\|"&lt;=", comparison_value: number}. An absent rule leaves the transition inert (no rule wired). |
| `compile_after` | boolean | no | Optional, default false; if true runs compile_anim_blueprint at the end |

**Returns:** `{ success: bool, anim_blueprint_path: string, machine_name: string, machine_already_existed: bool, states_created: int, states_skipped: int, transitions_created: int, transitions_updated: int, transitions_skipped: int, errors: [string], compiled: bool, compiled_after: bool }`

Request an async build of the PoseSearch index for a database

|---|---|---|---|
| `database_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UPoseSearchDatabase (required). |

**Returns:** `{ database_path, schema_path, schema_cardinality, animation_asset_count, wait_for_completion, result, success, in_progress, failed, message }`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove the property binding from one input pin of an AnimGraph node (inverse of set_anim_graph_node_pin_binding), dropping a stale binding without recreating the node. Returns was_bound, is_bound and cleared; an unbound pin gives cleared=false, not an error. Undoable; saves the AnimBP without recompiling (run compile_anim_blueprint).

| `node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the target UAnimGraphNode_* (from get_graph_nodes). |
| `pin_name` | string | yes | The bound property/pin name whose binding to clear (e.g. "TransformTrajectory"). |

| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph (optional; deep-resolved; default the top-level AnimGraph). |
| `anim_blueprint` | string | no | Alias of anim_blueprint_path, used only when anim_blueprint_path is absent or empty. |
| `blueprint_name` | string | no | Alias of anim_blueprint_path, used only when anim_blueprint_path and anim_blueprint are both absent or empty. |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, pin_name, was_bound, is_bound, cleared, saved }`

Remove every rule node from a transition's BoundGraph except the sink.

Remove EVERY FMotionWarpingTarget from a UMotionWarpingComponent in one call (there is no bulk engine API; use remove_warp_target for a single named target). Compile an Animation Blueprint synchronously and save its package, even when the compile fails; returns status (EBlueprintStatus name), is_up_to_date, has_error and the error and warning messages with their counts. *Destructive, idempotent.*

Switch the tick of a skeletal mesh component in the editor world (or the one the world param picks): despite the name, it only toggles component ticking and tick-when-paused. Returns the previous and current tick flags; nothing is marked dirty or saved.

*Destructive.*

Wire two AnimGraph pins (pose links AND data pins) using the graph's OWN schema. USE THIS INSTEAD OF connect_pins inside an AnimGraph: the generic connect_pins uses the K2 schema, which does not understand FPoseLink/FComponentSpacePoseLink pose pins, whereas this goes through UAnimationGraphSchema::TryCreateConnection so pose links connect correctly. Saves the ABP but does NOT recompile it -- run compile_anim_blueprint after your edits for runtime effect.

| `target_pin` | string | yes | Input pin name on the target node. |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph (optional, default the top-level AnimGraph). |

**Returns:** `{ connected, source_node_id, target_node_id, saved }`

## `connect_ik_goal_to_solver`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Connect an existing IK Rig goal to a solver, creating that solver's per-goal effector/settings, in one undo transaction, then save the asset.  This is the step that makes get_/set_ik_goal_settings work: a goal added via add_ik_goal is not attached to any solver until connected. Idempotent: re-connecting an already-connected goal is a success with already_connected:true, saved:false and a note, and nothing is saved, avoiding the duplicate the raw engine call would create. An unknown goal or out-of-range solver_index is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Content path to the IK Rig asset. |
| `goal_name` | string | yes | Name of an existing goal (created via add_ik_goal). |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | Index of the solver in the rig's solver stack. |

**Returns:** `{ ik_rig_path: string, goal_name: string, solver_index: int, connected: bool, already_connected: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

Copy a set of AnimGraph nodes (with internal FAnimNode settings + intra-selection wiring) between graphs. Equivalent to the editor's copy/paste: preserves each node's runtime struct properties and any links WITHIN the copied set (links to nodes outside the selection are dropped). Saves the destination ABP but does NOT recompile it -- run compile_anim_blueprint after your edits for runtime effect.

| `dst_graph` | string | no | Destination graph name (optional, default the top-level AnimGraph). |
| `offset_x` | number | no | X offset added to every pasted node (optional, default 0). |
| `offset_y` | number | no | Y offset added to every pasted node (optional, default 0). |

**Returns:** `{ copied_count, id_map:{old->new}, imported_nodes[], missing_node_ids[], saved }`

## `create_anim_montage`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create and save an empty-but-valid UAnimMontage asset under /Game. Idempotent: a UAnimMontage already at that path is returned unchanged with already_existed=true and saved=false, and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name (e.g. 'AM_Example'). |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Animation) |
| `slot_name` | string | no | Montage slot name (e.g. DefaultSlot) |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Asset path of the target Skeleton |

**Returns:** `{ name, package_path, asset_path, montage_path, skeleton_path, slot_names, slot_name, slot_count, section_count, created, already_existed, saved, save_error, message }`

## `create_anim_sequence`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create a UAnimSequence at package_path/anim_name bound to the USkeleton at skeleton_path (default the engine SkeletalCube_Skeleton) and save it; its data model gets frame_rate rounded to whole fps and round(length_seconds * fps) frames, but no bone tracks or curves. Idempotent: a UAnimSequence already at that path is returned unchanged (already_existed=true, saved=false, length and rate not applied) and nothing is saved; another asset class there or an unknown skeleton is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, and the new asset stays in memory only. Fill it with add_anim_bone_track or add_anim_float_curve; inspect it with get_anim_sequence_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_name` | string | yes | Asset name (no path). |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/MCP) |
| `length_seconds` | number | no | Sequence length in seconds (default 1.0) |
| `frame_rate` | number | no | Sampling frame rate in fps (default 30) |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Asset path of the target Skeleton |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, anim_name, skeleton, play_length, frame_rate, num_frames, success, saved, save_error, already_existed, message }`

## `create_blend_space`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create and save a UBlendSpace (or UBlendSpace1D) asset under /Game. Idempotent: a UBlendSpace already at that path is returned unchanged with already_existed=true and saved=false, and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name (e.g. 'BS_Example'). |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Animation) |
| `is_1d` | boolean | no | If true create a 1D BlendSpace, else 2D (default false) |
| `axis_name` | string | no | X-axis display name (default 'Speed') |
| `axis_min` | number | no | X-axis minimum value (default 0) |
| `axis_max` | number | no | X-axis maximum value (default 100) |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Asset path of the target Skeleton |

**Returns:** `{ name, package_path, asset_path, blend_space_path, is_1d, skeleton_path, axis_name, axis_min, axis_max, axis_grid_num, sample_count, created, already_existed, saved, save_error, message }`

## `create_control_rig_blueprint`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create a Control Rig Blueprint (non-modular) at package_path/name with UControlRigBlueprintFactory, compile it and save it. Idempotent: an existing Control Rig Blueprint there is returned unchanged (already_existed=true). Returns asset_path, generated_class, is_control_rig and saved; refused while PIE runs unless force is set.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | Content folder starting with "/", e.g. "/Game/Rigs"; a trailing slash is ignored |
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name of the Control Rig Blueprint, e.g. "CR_Hero" |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, name: string, generated_class: string, is_control_rig: bool, created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string }`

## `create_editable_skeletal_mesh`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Duplicate a skeletal mesh (default /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube) to package_path/skeletal_mesh_name in the project's content so it can be edited, creating the folder if needed. The copy keeps the source's skeleton (create_editable_skeleton makes a /Game skeleton) and is saved only when source control is enabled, otherwise follow with save_asset. Idempotent: a skeletal mesh already at that path is returned with created=false; any other asset there is an error. A source_mesh that is not a skeletal mesh is an error, and so is a destination that is engine content, under a read-only root or under no mounted root. duplicate_asset copies other asset types.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | Destination folder: a long package path used as given (/Game, /Game/MyGame or a project plugin mount), or a relative folder taken under /Game. |
| `skeletal_mesh_name` | string | yes | Name for the new skeletal mesh asset |
| `source_mesh` | string | no | Content path to source mesh to duplicate (default /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube) |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, skeletal_mesh_name: string, source_mesh: string, created: bool }`

## `create_editable_skeleton`

*Additive.*

Create an editable /Game skeleton by duplicating an engine skeleton

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | UE content folder, e.g. /Game/MyGame |
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name for the new skeleton |
| `source_skeleton` | string | no | Engine skeleton to duplicate, defaults to SkeletalCube_Skeleton |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, name: string, source: string, bone_count: int, created: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string }`

## `create_ik_retargeter`

*Additive.*

Create and save a UIKRetargeter asset wiring source + target IK Rigs. An existing retargeter at that path is rewired and saved when either rig differs; when it already uses both rigs nothing changes, nothing is saved (saved=false) and a note says so. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | UE content folder, e.g. /Game/MyGame |
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name for the new IK Retargeter |
| `source_ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the source UIKRigDefinition (copy FROM) |
| `target_ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the target UIKRigDefinition (copy TO) |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, name: string, source_ik_rig: string, target_ik_rig: string, created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `create_ik_rig`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create and save a UIKRigDefinition asset and set its source skeletal mesh.  Idempotent: an existing rig is loaded and only given the mesh, then saved, when it has another one; when it already has that mesh, or the mesh does not load or the engine refuses it (skeletal_mesh_set false), nothing changes, nothing is saved and a note says why. The default skeletal_mesh_path is /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | UE content folder, e.g. /Game/MyGame |
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name for the new IK Rig |
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | no | Optional USkeletalMesh asset path; defaults to /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, name: string, skeletal_mesh: string, skeletal_mesh_set: bool, created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `create_pose_asset`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create an empty UPoseAsset (no poses) at package_path/name, bound to the USkeleton at skeleton_path (default the engine SkeletalCube_Skeleton), and save it; no undo transaction. Idempotent: a UPoseAsset already at that path is returned untouched with already_existed=true and saved=false, even when bound to another skeleton, and nothing is saved. A name taken by another asset class or an unknown skeleton is an error, and a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Add poses with add_pose_to_pose_asset; to build one from animation frames use create_pose_asset_from_anim_sequence.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name (e.g. 'Pose_Example'). |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Animation) |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Asset path of the target Skeleton |

**Returns:** `{ name, package_path, asset_path, pose_asset_path, skeleton, num_poses, created, already_existed, saved, save_error, message }`

## `create_pose_asset_from_anim_sequence`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create a UPoseAsset built from a real UAnimSequence's frames and save it. Idempotent: a UPoseAsset already at that path is returned unchanged with already_existed=true and saved=false, and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pose_asset_name` | string | yes | Name for the new UPoseAsset. |
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Object path of the source UAnimSequence. |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Animation) |

**Returns:** `{ pose_asset_path, pose_asset_name, source_anim, skeleton_path, num_poses, created, success, already_existed, saved, save_error }`

## `create_pose_search_database`

*Additive.*

Create and save a UPoseSearchDatabase data asset bound to a UPoseSearchSchema

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name (e.g. 'PoseSearchDatabase_Example'). |
| `schema_path` | string | yes | Asset path of an existing UPoseSearchSchema (required). |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path (default /Game/MCP). |

**Returns:** `{ name, package_path, asset_path, database_path, schema_path, schema_cardinality, animation_asset_count, created, already_existed, saved, message }`

## `create_pose_search_schema`

*Additive.*

Create and save a UPoseSearchSchema data asset bound to a USkeleton

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name (e.g. 'PoseSearchSchema_Example'). |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path (default /Game/MCP). |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Asset path of the USkeleton (default /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton). |
| `sample_rate` | number | no | Schema SampleRate (int, ClampMin=1, ClampMax=240; default 30). |

**Returns:** `{ name, package_path, asset_path, schema_path, skeleton_path, sample_rate, schema_cardinality, channel_count, created, already_existed, saved, message }`

## `create_retarget_pose`

*Additive.*

Create a new retarget pose for editing in an IK Retargeter through its controller, then save the asset.  The engine makes the name unique, so read pose_name back. The pose is set as the current pose after creation, ready for bone rotation edits via set_retarget_pose_bone_rotation. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_retargeter_path` | string | yes | Content path to the IK Retargeter asset. |
| `pose_name` | string | yes | Name for the new retarget pose |
| `source_or_target` | string | no | Optional "Source" or "Target" scope; defaults to "Target" |

**Returns:** `{ ik_retargeter_path: string, pose_name: string, source_or_target: string, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `create_skeletal_mesh_morph_target`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Register a new morph target on a skeletal mesh asset in memory only, for the rest of the editor session: it is never saved (persisted_to_disk is always false), and a mesh rebuild or reload drops any morph the mesh's imported source data does not contain. Each LOD gets one tiny seed delta on vertex 0 so the morph counts as valid; write real deltas with set_morph_target_deltas. Marks the mesh dirty. Idempotent: an existing name returns created=false and already_exists=true.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset (e.g. /Game/MyGame/SKM_Example) |
| `morph_target_name` | string | yes | Name for the new morph target |

**Returns:** `{ morph_target_name: string, skeletal_mesh_path: string, created: bool, persisted_to_disk: bool, total_morph_targets: int, note: string }`

## `delete_montage_section`

*Destructive.*

Delete the first composite section with that name (FName match, case ignored) from a UAnimMontage and save it; a missing name is a success with removed=false and nothing saved. Links from other sections (NextSectionName) are not updated. Returns removed_index, section_count and the remaining sections. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'). |
| `section_name` | string | yes | Name of the FCompositeSection to remove; compared as an FName, so case is ignored. |

**Returns:** `{ montage_path, section_name, removed_index?, already_existed, removed, section_count, sections[], saved, save_error, message }`

## `disconnect_anim_graph_pins`

*Destructive.*

Break AnimGraph pin links: a specific source->target link, or ALL links on the source pin. Use the specific form to insert a node into an existing chain (break A->B, then wire A->N and N->B). Saves the ABP but does NOT recompile it -- run compile_anim_blueprint after your edits for runtime effect.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Path/name of the UAnimBlueprint. |
| `source_node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the source node. |
| `source_pin` | string | yes | Pin name on the source node. |
| `target_node_id` | string | no | NodeGuid of the target node (optional; if omitted, breaks ALL links on source_pin). |
| `target_pin` | string | no | Pin name on the target node (optional; required if target_node_id is given). |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph (optional, default the top-level AnimGraph). |

**Returns:** `{ disconnected, broke_all, source_node_id, source_pin, saved }`

## `disconnect_ik_goal_from_solver`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Disconnect a goal from a solver, removing that solver's per-goal effector/settings, through the IK Rig controller (one undo transaction), then save the asset.  Inverse of connect_ik_goal_to_solver. Idempotent: disconnecting a goal that isn't connected is a success with was_connected:false, saved:false and a note, and nothing is saved. An out-of-range solver_index is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Content path to the IK Rig asset. |
| `goal_name` | string | yes | Name of the goal. |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | Index of the solver in the rig's solver stack. |

**Returns:** `{ ik_rig_path: string, goal_name: string, solver_index: int, connected: bool, was_connected: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `duplicate_anim_sequence`

*Additive.*

Copy a UAnimSequence to a new asset package_path/new_name with the same skeleton (StaticDuplicateObject) and save it; a name already taken by any asset, in memory or on disk (the source included), is refused and nothing is touched. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, and the copy stays in memory only. Returns duplicate_path and duplicate_class. For other asset types use duplicate_asset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the source UAnimSequence. |
| `new_name` | string | yes | Name of the new duplicate. |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/MCP) |

**Returns:** `{ source_path, duplicate_path, duplicate_class, saved, save_error }`

## `edit_anim_notify`

*Destructive.*

Edit an existing FAnimNotifyEvent on a UAnimSequence (identified by name + occurrence) in an undo transaction and save it. No editable field is an error before anything changes; edits that leave the event as it is are a success with applied=false, applied_count 0 and saved=false, and the sequence is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `animation_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UAnimSequence. |
| `notify_name` | string | yes | NotifyName of the event to edit (FName). Names are not unique; see occurrence_index. |
| `occurrence_index` | number | no | Zero-based index AMONG events sharing notify_name (default 0) |
| `time` | number | no | New trigger time in seconds (FAnimNotifyEvent::SetTime). Optional. |
| `duration` | number | no | New duration in seconds (FAnimNotifyEvent::SetDuration; meaningful for notify-state). Optional. |
| `trigger_chance` | number | no | New NotifyTriggerChance in [0,1]. Optional. |
| `trigger_weight_threshold` | number | no | New TriggerWeightThreshold. Optional. |
| `montage_tick_type` | string | no | New MontageTickType: 'Queued' or 'BranchingPoint'. Optional. |
| `track_index` | number | no | New TrackIndex (zero-based). Optional. |

**Returns:** `{ animation_path, notify_name, occurrence_index, matched_count, notify, applied_count, applied, saved, save_error, message }`

## `edit_blendspace_sample`

*Destructive.*

Edit a blend sample (by index): blend value and/or animation. At least one of blend_value / animation_path is required; both are individually optional so you can retime a sample without touching its animation, or swap the animation without moving it. A sample that already has those values is a success with value_edited=false, animation_replaced=false and saved=false, and the blend space is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blendspace_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UBlendSpace. |
| `index` | number | yes | Index of the sample to edit. |
| `blend_value` | any | no | New blend position: single number (1D) or array of up to 3 numbers (optional). |
| `animation_path` | string | no | Full asset path to a UAnimSequence to replace the sample's animation (optional). |

**Returns:** `{ blendspace_path, index, value_edited, animation_replaced, num_samples, samples, saved, save_error, message }`

## `evaluate_pose_search_query`

*Read-only.*

Run a live motion-matching query on a PIE/Game actor against a loaded UPoseSearchDatabase (UPoseSearchLibrary::MotionMatch) and return the best-match asset + search cost, plus the query trajectory. Diagnoses why a chooser returns null. Best-effort: per-channel cost is not exposed by the BlueprintPure result.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `database_path` | string | yes | UPoseSearchDatabase asset path to search (required). |
| `world` | string | no | Which world to resolve: absent (default) = prefer the live PIE/Game world \| 'server' (the PIE world with authority) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' \| 'pie'/'game' force the live session (errors if none running) \| 'editor' forces the editor world. |
| `actor_name` | string | no | Actor name or label whose AnimInstance drives the query. Omitted = the first player controller's pawn. |
| `pose_history_name` | string | no | Tag of the PoseSearchHistoryCollector anim-graph node used to build the query (default 'PoseHistory'). |
| `max_trajectory_samples` | number | no | Cap on emitted query trajectory samples (&lt;=0 = all; default 0). |

**Returns:** `{ world_mode, actor_name, actor_resolved, anim_instance_class, pose_history_name, pose_history_found, database_path, query_trajectory_samples[], trajectory_sample_count, is_trajectory_empty, has_match, best_match_asset, best_match_database, best_cost, selected_time, is_continuing_pose_search, wanted_play_rate, is_mirrored, is_looping, per_channel_cost[], note, world_name, world_package, world_type, net_mode, pie_instance }`

## `get_active_montages`

*Read-only.*

Report the AnimMontage(s) currently playing on a live PIE actor's skeletal mesh (useful for blend-out debugging).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor` | string | yes | Name, label, or full path of a live actor (resolved in the PIE world by default). |
| `component` | string | no | Optional skeletal mesh component name; defaults to the actor's primary USkeletalMeshComponent. |
| `world` | string | no | Which world to resolve the actor in: absent/'pie' (default, ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) \| 'server' (the PIE world with authority) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' \| 'editor' \| 'game' (alias of 'pie'). |

**Returns:** `{ actor, actor_name, component, world, anim_instance_class, montage_count, is_any_montage_playing, top_montage_id, enumeration, montages: [{ index, montage_path, montage_name, is_top, current_section, position, normalized_position, length, play_rate, blend_weight, desired_weight, blend_time, is_playing, is_active, instance_id, slots:[string] }], world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }`

## `get_anim_asset_info`

*Read-only.*

Load any animation asset and report its class, skeleton and asset_type (montage, composite, pose, sequence, blendspace or animation_asset) plus the counts of that type: sections/slots/notifies, segments, poses/tracks/curves, length, samples. Read-only; get_montage_info, get_anim_sequence_info and get_blendspace_samples give detail.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_path` | string | yes | Path to the animation asset (UAnimMontage, UAnimComposite, UPoseAsset, UAnimSequence, or UBlendSpace) |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, class, skeleton, num_segments, num_poses, section_count, slot_count, notify_count, sequence_length, rate_scale, num_tracks, num_curves, sample_count, asset_type }`

## `get_anim_blueprint_info`

*Read-only.*

Read an Animation Blueprint without compiling or changing it: target skeleton, parent and generated class, is_anim_instance, is_template, graph_count, and the state machines of its top-level AnimGraph with their state counts (conduits not counted). list_anim_state_machines scans every function graph.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Path to the UAnimBlueprint asset |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, target_skeleton: string, target_skeleton_set: bool, parent_class: string, generated_class: string, is_anim_instance: bool, is_template: bool, graph_count: int, state_machine_count: int, state_machines: [{ name: string, state_count: int }] }`

*Read-only.*

Read one curve of a UAnimSequence without changing it: for a float curve its flags, num_keys and keys as time/value pairs; for a transform curve only flags and a summed num_keys. found=false (still a success) when the curve does not exist.

|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UAnimSequence |
| `curve_name` | string | yes | Name of the curve to read |
| `curve_type` | string | no | Curve type to target: float (default) or transform |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, curve_name, curve_type, found, num_keys, flags, time, value, keys }`

List the bone tracks, float curves, and transform curves on a UAnimSequence

| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |

Read the internal FAnimNode struct of an AnimGraphNode as typed JSON (the runtime settings, not the K2 pin surface get_graph_nodes reports). Use it to mirror a reference ABP's settings when grafting nodes: Pose History PoseCount/CollectorName, Slot SlotName, blend params...

## `get_anim_notifies`

*Read-only.*

List the notify events of a UAnimSequence without changing it: name, trigger time, duration, track_index and the notify_class or notify_state_class of each, plus num_notifies. Use get_notify_track_names for track names and get_montage_info for the notifies of a montage.

|---|---|---|---|
| `animation_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UAnimSequence. |

## `get_anim_sequence_info`

*Read-only.*

Read a UAnimSequence without changing it: skeleton, play_length, frame_rate, num_frames, bone track and float curve counts from its data model, num_sync_markers, enable_root_motion, retarget_source and ref_pose_seq. Use get_anim_curve_names for the track and curve names.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, skeleton, play_length, frame_rate, num_frames, num_bone_tracks, num_float_curves, num_sync_markers, enable_root_motion, success }`

## `get_anim_state_machine_info`

*Read-only.*

Read the nodes of one state machine of an Animation Blueprint without compiling or changing it: state_count counts the states, conduit_count the conduits and transition_count the transitions; states lists every state, conduit and alias node with its kind (class name) and graph position, transitions excluded.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimBlueprint |
| `state_machine_name` | string | yes | Name of the state machine |

**Returns:** `{ state_machine, state_count, conduit_count, transition_count, states:[{name,kind,x,y}] }`

## `get_animation_blueprint_info`

*Read-only.*

Find an Animation Blueprint in the Asset Registry and report its object path, class, package, is_loaded and the size and timestamp of its .uasset on disk. With load_full_data it also loads the asset and adds the target skeleton, its bone count, the generated class and is_abstract. Read-only. blueprint_name takes an object path, a package path or a short name searched under /Game (the first match when several share it); no match is an error. For parent class, graphs and state machines use get_anim_blueprint_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name or full path of the Animation Blueprint asset |
| `load_full_data` | boolean | no | When true, loads the asset and reports target skeleton, generated class, and bone count (optional, default false) |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name: string, blueprint_path: string, blueprint_class: string, package_name: string, is_loaded: bool, file_size_bytes: number, file_size_kb: number, file_size_mb: number, last_modified: string, loaded_successfully: bool?, is_valid: bool?, target_skeleton: string?, skeleton_bone_count: number?, has_target_skeleton: bool?, generated_class: string?, is_abstract: bool?, load_error: string? }`

## `get_blendspace_samples`

*Read-only.*

Read every sample of a UBlendSpace or UBlendSpace1D in index order (animation path, blend_x/blend_y/blend_z, rate_scale) plus num_samples and the per-axis input smoothing under interpolation. Read-only; change samples with add_blendspace_sample, edit_blendspace_sample or remove_blendspace_sample.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blendspace_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UBlendSpace. |

**Returns:** `{ animation, blend_x, blend_y, blend_z, rate_scale, blendspace_path, num_samples, samples }`

## `get_bone_transform`

*Read-only.*

Read the LOCAL reference-pose transform of a bone (parent-relative, not component space). Exact inverse of set_bone_transform: it reads the same raw ref-pose array that one writes, so a read-modify-write round trip is lossless.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | Path to the USkeleton asset |
| `bone_name` | string | yes | Bone to read |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, bone_name, bone_index, found, location:[x,y,z], rotation:[p,y,r], scale:[x,y,z], bone_count, op: "get_bone_transform" }`

## `get_ik_bone_settings`

*Read-only.*

Get bone-specific settings for a bone within a solver.  FullBodyIK returns snake_case keys (rotation/position stiffness, axis limits Free/Limited/Locked, min/max angles, preferred angles); StretchLimb (the only other solver with per-bone settings) is serialized generically (camelCase: squashDirection vector). Only FullBodyIK and StretchLimb support per-bone settings; others return a `note`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Content path to the IK Rig asset. |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | Index of the solver. |
| `bone_name` | string | yes | Name of the bone to query settings for. |

**Returns:** `{ ik_rig_path: string, solver_index: int, bone_name: string, settings: object }`

## `get_ik_goal_settings`

*Read-only.*

Get goal-specific settings for a goal connected to a solver.  FullBodyIK returns snake_case keys (chain_depth, strength_alpha, pull_chain_alpha, pin_rotation); BodyMover (the only other solver with per-goal settings) is serialized generically (camelCase: influenceMultiplier, boneName). The goal must be connected to the solver first (connect_ik_goal_to_solver), else a `note` explains that. Solvers without per-goal settings return a `note`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Content path to the IK Rig asset. |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | Index of the solver. |
| `goal_name` | string | yes | Name of the goal to query settings for. |

**Returns:** `{ ik_rig_path: string, solver_index: int, goal_name: string, settings: object }`

## `get_ik_retarget_chain_details`

*Read-only.*

Get detailed info about a retarget chain: start/end bones, goal name.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset |
| `chain_name` | string | yes | Name of the retarget chain |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, chain_name: string, found: bool, start_bone: string, end_bone: string, goal_name: string }`

## `get_ik_retargeter_info`

*Read-only.*

Read the global structure of an IK Retargeter via its controller: source/target IK Rigs, the op-stack, per-op chain mappings, and the current poses.  Read-only. Chain mappings are per-op in 5.6+ (there is no global RootSettings on the UIKRetargeter in 5.8; detailed root/global settings live inside the ops themselves).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_retargeter_path` | string | yes | Content path to the UIKRetargeter asset. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, source_ik_rig: string, target_ik_rig: string, op_count: int, ops: [{ op_index, op_name, enabled, parent_op, op_type }], chain_mappings: [{ op_name, target_chain, source_chain }], source: { current_pose, pelvis_bone, root_offset: {x,y,z} }, target: { current_pose, pelvis_bone, root_offset: {x,y,z} } }`

## `get_ik_rig_info`

*Read-only.*

Read an IK Rig asset: its skeletal mesh, the number of solvers, and every goal and retarget chain. Read-only; solvers are counted, not listed: get_ik_solver_details reads one by index.

| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset |

## `get_ik_solver_bones`

*Read-only.*

Read the start and end bone of one solver in an IK Rig asset, chosen by its 0-based position in the solver stack. Read-only; an out-of-range solver_index or a rig that does not load is an error. A solver type without an end bone returns "None" as end_bone. get_ik_solver_details adds the type, enabled state and connected goals; set_ik_solver_bones writes the bones.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | 0-based solver index |

## `get_ik_solver_details`

*Read-only.*

Read one solver of an IK Rig asset by its 0-based stack index: solver_type (the solver struct name, e.g. "IKRigFullBodyIKSolver"), unique_name ("&lt;index+1> - &lt;display name>"), enabled, start and end bone, and the names of the goals connected to it. Read-only; an out-of-range solver_index or a rig that does not load is an error. Use get_ik_solver_bones for just the bones, get_ik_solver_settings for its tunables, get_ik_rig_info for the goals and chains of the whole rig.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |

| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | 0-based solver index |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, solver_index: int, solver_type: string, unique_name: string, enabled: bool, start_bone: string, end_bone: string, connected_goal_count: int, connected_goals: [string] }`

## `get_ik_solver_settings`

*Read-only.*

Get detailed solver-specific settings for a solver in an IK Rig.  Returns all solver-level parameters for the specified solver. FullBodyIK uses curated snake_case keys; every other solver type (Limb/Pole/BodyMover/SetTransform/StretchLimb) is serialized generically from its live settings struct (camelCase property names).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Content path to the IK Rig asset. |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | Index of the solver in the rig's solver stack. |

Read back the vertex deltas of a morph target on a specific LOD (inverse of set_morph_target_deltas).

## `get_pose_search_runtime_state`

*Read-only.*

Read-only report of the live motion-matching state on a PIE/Game actor (why a chooser returns null): its AnimInstance, its MotionTrajectory samples, whether a PoseSearchHistoryCollector node named pose_history_name exists, and (optionally) the target database's schema/channels.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `world` | string | no | Which world to resolve: absent (default) = prefer the live PIE/Game world, else the editor world \| 'server' (the PIE world with authority -- what a server-driven character lives in) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' \| 'pie'/'game' force the live session (errors if none running) \| 'editor' forces the editor world. |
| `actor_name` | string | no | Actor name or label to inspect. Omitted = the first player controller's pawn (the locally-controlled character). |

| `max_trajectory_samples` | number | no | Cap on emitted trajectory samples (&lt;=0 = all; default 0). |

**Returns:** `{ world_mode, actor_name, actor_resolved, actor_resolved_by, skeletal_mesh_component, anim_instance_class, pose_history_name, pose_history_found, trajectory:{found,component,property,sample_count,is_trajectory_empty,samples[]}, is_trajectory_empty, database?:{database_path,schema_path,schema_cardinality,channel_count,channels[],animation_asset_count}, note, world_name, world_package, world_type, net_mode, pie_instance }`

## `link_montage_sections`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Chain one montage section to the next by setting its NextSectionName.  add_montage_section creates sections but never links them; this writes FCompositeSection::NextSectionName so playback flows section -> next. Pass next_section_name "" or "None" to clear the link. Done in an undo transaction, then saved. Idempotent: the link the section already has is a success with changed=false and saved=false, and the montage is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'). |
| `section_name` | string | yes | Name of the existing section whose link to set. |
| `next_section_name` | string | yes | Name of the existing section to play next (or "" / "None" to clear). |

**Returns:** `{ montage_path, section_name, next_section_name, linked, changed, section_count, sections, saved, save_error, message }`

*Read-only.*

List the state machine nodes at the top level of every function graph of an Animation Blueprint (the AnimGraph included), read-only and without compiling: count and state_machines [{name, graph_name}]. Machines nested inside states are not listed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimBlueprint |

**Returns:** `{ count, state_machines: [{name, graph_name}] }`

*Read-only.*

List every FMotionWarpingTarget on an actor's UMotionWarpingComponent. Read-only: wraps GetWarpTargets() (TConstArrayView&lt;FMotionWarpingTarget>). Each entry reports the FName, the static location/rotation, the optional component reference (via path or null), the optional bone name, the b_follow_component flag, the location/rotation offsets, and the location_offset_direction enum integer.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_path` | string | yes | Full editor path or short name of the actor. |

**Returns:** `{ actor_path: string, warp_target_count: int, warp_targets: array }`

## `move_ik_solver_in_stack`

*Destructive.*

Move the solver at from_index so that it ends up at to_index (both 0-based positions in the solver stack) of an IK Rig asset through the IK Rig controller (one undo transaction), then save the asset. An index outside the stack is an error and nothing moves; from_index equal to to_index is not an error but moved false, saved false and a note, with nothing saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset |
| `from_index` | number | yes | Source 0-based solver index |
| `to_index` | number | yes | Target 0-based solver index, below the solver count |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, from_index: int, to_index: int, moved: bool, solver_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `play_animation`

*Destructive.*

Play an AnimMontage on a skeletal mesh component with UAnimInstance::Montage_Play at play_rate, then jump to start_section if playback started. Editor world unless the world param says otherwise; the component needs an anim instance. playing/success mean Montage_Play returned a length above 0.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `component_name` | string | yes | Object name of the USkeletalMeshComponent, e.g. "CharacterMesh0", case-insensitive; the first actor in the world that has one with that name wins |
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the AnimMontage (e.g. '/Game/Animations/MyMontage.MyMontage') |
| `play_rate` | number | no | Playback rate multiplier (optional, default 1.0) |
| `start_section` | string | no | Name of the section to jump to after play starts (optional) |
| `world` | string | no | Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) \| 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) \| 'server' (the PIE world with authority) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' \| 'game' (alias of 'pie'). |

**Returns:** `{ component_name: string, montage_path: string, montage_name: string, playing: bool, play_rate: number, montage_length: number, return_value: number, success: bool, start_section: string?, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }`

## `refresh_anim_montage_cache`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Re-run UAnimMontage::RefreshCacheData on a UAnimMontage in an undo transaction (it sorts the notifies, moves a notify off a missing or overlapping notify track, adding tracks as needed, and rebuilds the branching point markers) and save it. Idempotent: when the refresh rewrites none of those fields the reply is a success with refreshed=false and saved=false, the montage keeps the dirty state it had and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'). |

**Returns:** `{ montage_path, refreshed, sequence_length, slot_count, section_count, saved, save_error, message }`

## `reimport_anim_sequence`

*Destructive.*

Reimport a UAnimSequence, or any reimportable asset (the class is not checked), from source_file_path or its first recorded source via FReimportManager, automated (no dialogs) and unsaved. A missing source is refused before the reimport, which would crash the editor on it, and a reimport the handler reports as failed is a failure too: both make success false with reimported=false, and the missing source a note.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UAnimSequence |
| `source_file_path` | string | no | Absolute path of the file to reimport from on disk (e.g. "D:/Art/Walk.fbx"); defaults to the first source file recorded in the asset import data. |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, source_file_path, reimported, source_validated, note? }`
