|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset |
| `socket_name` | string | yes | Name of the socket to remove |

**Returns:** `{ socket_name: string, skeletal_mesh_path: string, removed: bool, already_removed: bool, socket_count: int }`

## `remove_socket_from_skeleton_asset`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove a socket from the socket list of a USkeleton asset and save it. Idempotent: a missing socket returns removed false and already_absent true without saving. Returns socket_count and the remaining socket_names; sockets that exist only on a skeletal mesh are untouched (use remove_skeletal_mesh_socket).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | USkeleton asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton". |
| `socket_name` | string | yes | Name of the socket to remove (case-insensitive). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, socket_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, socket_count: int, socket_names: [string], saved: bool }`

## `remove_virtual_bone`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove a virtual bone from a USkeleton asset, named directly or found by its source and target bones, then save. Idempotent: no match returns removed false and already_absent true without saving. Returns the remaining virtual_bone_names; a failed save returns success false.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | USkeleton asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton". |
| `virtual_bone_name` | string | no | Full virtual bone name with its "VB " prefix, e.g. "VB pelvis_hand_r"; when given, source_bone and target_bone are ignored. |
| `source_bone` | string | no | Source bone name; used with target_bone to resolve the virtual bone when virtual_bone_name is omitted. |
| `target_bone` | string | no | Target bone name; used with source_bone to resolve the virtual bone when virtual_bone_name is omitted. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, virtual_bone_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, virtual_bone_count: int, virtual_bone_names: [string], saved: bool }`

## `remove_warp_target`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove a FMotionWarpingTarget from a UMotionWarpingComponent by FName. Wraps UMotionWarpingComponent::RemoveWarpTarget(name) which returns the count of entries removed (0 or 1; the array is keyed by FName). Idempotent: removing a non-existent target returns count:0 without raising an error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_path` | string | yes | Full editor path or short name of the actor. |
| `target_name` | string | yes | FName identifier of the warp target to remove. |

**Returns:** `{ actor_path: string, target_name: string, removed_count: int, warp_target_count: int }`

## `rename_anim_curve`

*Destructive.*

Rename a float or transform curve on a UAnimSequence through its data controller (one undo step) and save it; errors when the source curve does not exist or the rename is refused. The same name for both is a success with renamed=false, saved=false and a note, and nothing is written or saved. Any curve_type other than transform means float. Returns renamed and saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UAnimSequence |
| `old_curve_name` | string | yes | Name of the existing curve to rename, as listed by get_anim_curve_names. |
| `new_curve_name` | string | yes | Name the curve gets after the rename. |
| `curve_type` | string | no | Curve type to target: float (default) or transform |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, old_curve_name, new_curve_name, renamed, saved, save_error, note? }`

## `rename_bone`

*Destructive.*

Rename a bone in the reference skeleton of a USkeleton asset and save it. Fails with an error when old_name is not a bone or new_name is already taken; skeletal meshes and animations that use the old name are not updated. A failed save returns success false.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | USkeleton asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton". |
| `old_name` | string | yes | Current bone name; must exist in the reference skeleton. |
| `new_name` | string | yes | Desired new bone name (must not already exist) |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, old_name, new_name, renamed: true, not_found: false, already_used: false, bone_count, saved, save_error?, op: "rename_bone" }`

## `rename_ik_retarget_chain`

*Destructive.*

Rename a retarget chain of an IK Rig asset through the IK Rig controller (one undo transaction) and save it. The engine makes the new name unique, so read new_name back; an unknown chain_name is not an error but returns renamed false, saved false and a note, with nothing saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | IK Rig (UIKRigDefinition) asset path, e.g. "/Game/Retarget/IK_Hero". |
| `chain_name` | string | yes | Current name of the retarget chain, as get_ik_rig_info lists it. |
| `new_name` | string | yes | Requested new name; the engine may add a suffix to keep it unique. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, old_name: string, new_name: string, renamed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `rename_montage_section`

*Destructive.*

Rename an existing FCompositeSection on a UAnimMontage by zero-based section_index, in an undo transaction, and save it. The name the section already has (FName match, case ignored) is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and the montage is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'). |
| `section_index` | number | yes | Zero-based index into CompositeSections (use get_montage_info first to list). |
| `new_name` | string | yes | New FName for the section. |

**Returns:** `{ montage_path, section_index, old_name, new_name, section_count, sections, applied, saved, save_error, message }`

## `rename_pose_in_pose_asset`

*Destructive.*

Rename an existing named pose in a UPoseAsset (UPoseAsset::ModifyPoseName) in an undo transaction and save it; renamed is measured by reading the pose names back. An unknown old_pose_name, a new_pose_name another pose already has, or a rename the engine does not take is an error with nothing saved; the same name for both is a success with renamed=false and saved=false, and nothing is modified or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pose_asset_path` | string | yes | Path to the UPoseAsset. |
| `old_pose_name` | string | yes | Current name of the pose to rename. |
| `new_pose_name` | string | yes | New name for the pose. |

**Returns:** `{ pose_asset_path, old_pose_name, new_pose_name, renamed, contains_new, contains_old, num_poses, pose_names, saved, save_error, message }`

## `rename_rig_element`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Rename an element in a Control Rig's hierarchy.  Idempotent: renaming to the current name is a no-op ({ renamed:false, already_named:true }). The engine disambiguates name collisions with a numeric suffix rather than failing, reported honestly via name_adjusted.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UControlRigBlueprint asset |
| `element_type` | string | yes | Element type ("Bone"/"Null"/"Control"/"Curve"/"Socket"/"Connector") |
| `element_name` | string | yes | Current name of the element to rename |
| `new_name` | string | yes | Desired new name for the element |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, old_name: string, element_key: string, element_type: string, renamed: bool, already_named: bool, name_adjusted: bool, bone_count: int, null_count: int, control_count: int, curve_count: int, other_count: int, total: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }`

## `rename_skeletal_mesh_morph_target`

*Destructive.*

Rename a morph target on a skeletal mesh asset and save the mesh. Fails if old_name is not a morph target of the mesh or new_name already exists; a failed save also returns an error although the rename stays in memory. Returns old_name, new_name and renamed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Skeletal mesh asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero". |
| `old_name` | string | yes | Current morph target name, as get_skeletal_mesh_morph_targets lists it. |
| `new_name` | string | yes | New morph target name; must not already exist on the mesh. |

**Returns:** `{ old_name: string, new_name: string, skeletal_mesh_path: string, renamed: bool }`

## `rename_skeletal_mesh_socket`

*Destructive.*

Rename a socket on a skeletal mesh (and its skeleton twin).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset |
| `old_name` | string | yes | Current name of the socket |
| `new_name` | string | yes | New name for the socket |

**Returns:** `{ old_name: string, new_name: string, skeletal_mesh_path: string, renamed: bool, already_renamed: bool, socket_count: int }`

## `scaffold_aim_offset_blend_space`

*Additive.*

Create a UAimOffsetBlendSpace for a skeleton at package_path/asset_name and save it, or re-save the one already there (already_existed=true); a failed save still succeeds with saved=false. Yaw/pitch ranges and grid counts are only echoed, not written: set axes with set_blendspace_properties.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | Content folder for the new asset, e.g. /Game/Animation/AimOffsets (a trailing slash is ignored). |
| `asset_name` | string | yes | Name of the aim offset asset (e.g. "AO_Rifle"); the object path becomes package_path/asset_name.asset_name. |
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the USkeleton the new aim offset targets (e.g. "/Game/Characters/Mannequin/SK_Mannequin_Skeleton"); a reused asset keeps its own skeleton. |
| `yaw_min` | number | no | Yaw lower bound echoed in the reply (default -90.0 degrees); not written to the asset. |
| `yaw_max` | number | no | Yaw upper bound echoed in the reply (default 90.0); not written to the asset. |
| `pitch_min` | number | no | Pitch lower bound echoed in the reply (default -90.0); not written to the asset. |
| `pitch_max` | number | no | Pitch upper bound echoed in the reply (default 90.0); not written to the asset. |
| `num_grid_points_yaw` | number | no | Yaw grid divisions echoed in the reply (default 4); not written to the asset. |
| `num_grid_points_pitch` | number | no | Pitch grid divisions echoed in the reply (default 4); not written to the asset. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, skeleton_path, yaw_min, yaw_max, pitch_min, pitch_max, num_grid_points_yaw, num_grid_points_pitch, already_existed, saved, note? }`

## `scaffold_blend_space_2d`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create a UBlendSpace (2D) asset for parameter-driven animation blending (e.g. Speed x Direction). Idempotent on re-run; axis metadata left at engine defaults (set the protected axis fields afterwards with set_blendspace_properties).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | /Game/... folder for the new asset (required) |
| `asset_name` | string | yes | Display name (required) |
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | USkeleton the BS targets (required) |
| `axis_x_label` | string | no | Optional X-axis display name (default "X"); engine field is protected so visible only after editor opens the asset. |
| `axis_y_label` | string | no | Optional Y-axis display name (default "Y"); same engine protection caveat. |
| `min_x` | number | no | Optional X axis lower bound (default 0); recorded in response but not written to asset. |
| `max_x` | number | no | Optional X axis upper bound (default 100); same caveat as above. |
| `min_y` | number | no | Optional Y axis lower bound (default 0) |
| `max_y` | number | no | Optional Y axis upper bound (default 100) |
| `num_grid_points_x` | number | no | Optional X grid density (default 4) |
| `num_grid_points_y` | number | no | Optional Y grid density (default 4) |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, skeleton_path, axis_x_label, axis_y_label, x_axis_range, y_axis_range, num_grid_points_x, num_grid_points_y, already_existed, saved, note? }`

## `scaffold_locomotion_animbp`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create or update a character Animation Blueprint with a "Locomotion" state machine + Idle/Walk/Run states + bidirectional transitions between them. Idempotent: re-running on an existing AnimBP returns the existing scaffold.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | UE content folder, e.g. "/Game/MyGame". |
| `asset_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name, e.g. "ABP_PlayerLocomotion". |
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | Path to the target USkeleton. |
| `machine_name` | string | no | Optional state machine name (default "Locomotion"). |
| `states` | array | no | Optional list of state names to add (default ["Idle", "Walk", "Run"]). |
| `add_transitions` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default true). Add Idle&lt;->Walk and Walk&lt;->Run transitions. |

**Returns:** `{ anim_blueprint_path, package_path, skeleton_path, machine_name, state_count, transition_count, already_existed, saved }`

## `scale_anim_curve`

*Destructive.*

Retime a FLOAT curve on a UAnimSequence through its data controller (one undo step), then save the package: every key TIME becomes (t - origin) * factor + origin, and the key VALUES are left untouched -- this stretches/compresses a curve in time, it does not scale its amplitude. FLOAT-CURVE ONLY: a name that is not a float curve of the sequence, a transform curve included, is an error and nothing is written. A retime that moves no key (factor 1, no keys, or every key at the origin) is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `curve_name` | string | yes | Name of the float curve. |
| `factor` | number | no | Scale factor applied to each key TIME (default 1.0). |
| `origin` | number | no | Time origin the key times are scaled about (default 0.0). |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, curve_name, origin, factor, num_keys, applied, saved, save_error, message }`

## `set_anim_additive_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the additive-animation type and base pose on a UAnimSequence in an undo transaction and save it. Settings the sequence already has are a success with changed=false and saved=false, and the sequence is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Object path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `additive_anim_type` | string | no | Additive type: LocalSpaceBase\|RotationOffsetMeshSpace\|None (default LocalSpaceBase) |
| `ref_pose_type` | string | no | Base pose type: RefPose\|AnimScaled\|AnimFrame\|LocalAnimFrame\|None (default RefPose) |
| `ref_frame_index` | number | no | Frame index used for the base pose (default 0) |
| `ref_pose_anim_path` | string | no | Object path of the reference UAnimSequence for the base pose (optional) |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, additive_anim_type, ref_pose_type, ref_frame_index, ref_pose_anim_set, changed, success, saved, save_error, message? }`

## `set_anim_bone_track_keys`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Replace the keys of one bone track of a UAnimSequence with the given per-key transforms (translation, rotation, scale: real pose data, not identity), adding the track when it is missing, through its data controller as one undo step, then save the package; num_keys_readback and first_key are read back from the data model. A track that already holds exactly these keys (the stored track data comes out unchanged, measured with the data model GUID) is a success with changed=false and saved=false, the package keeps the dirty state it had and nothing is saved. A bone_name the sequence's skeleton does not have is an error and nothing is written; an omitted bone_name targets the root bone. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Identity keys: add_anim_bone_track.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `keys` | array | yes | Array of per-key transforms: { translation:[x,y,z], rotation:[pitch,yaw,roll] (deg), scale:[x,y,z] }. translation default [0,0,0], rotation default [0,0,0], scale default [1,1,1]. |
| `bone_name` | string | no | Name of a bone of the skeleton of the sequence; omitted or empty means the root bone. |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, bone_name, num_keys, num_keys_readback, num_bone_tracks, first_key:{translation,rotation_euler}, changed, success, saved, save_error, message }`

## `set_anim_curve_color`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the editor display color of a FLOAT curve on a UAnimSequence through its data controller (one undo step), then save the package (cosmetic: it tints the curve in the editor, it does not affect evaluation). FLOAT-CURVE ONLY: a name that is not a float curve of the sequence, a transform curve included, is an error and nothing is written. The color the curve already has is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `curve_name` | string | yes | Name of the float curve. |
| `color` | array | no | RGBA color as [r, g, b, a] in 0..1 (default [1,1,1,1]). |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, curve_name, color, applied, saved, save_error, message }`

## `set_anim_curve_comment`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the author comment of a FLOAT curve on a UAnimSequence through its data controller (one undo step), then save the package (metadata only; it does not affect evaluation). FLOAT-CURVE ONLY: a name that is not a float curve of the sequence, a transform curve included, is an error and nothing is written. The comment the curve already has (case-sensitive) is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `curve_name` | string | yes | Name of the float curve. |
| `comment` | string | no | Comment string to set (default empty). |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, curve_name, comment, applied, saved, save_error, message }`

## `set_anim_curve_interp_mode`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Replace the curve flags (the EAnimAssetCurveFlags bitmask) of an existing float or transform curve on a UAnimSequence with one flag, in an undo transaction, then save the package. Despite the name it changes no key interpolation or tangents: linear and editable both set Editable; metadata, drive_track and disabled set those flags. interp_mode is required; an unknown mode, curve or sequence is an error, and any curve_type other than transform means float. old_flags and new_flags are the bitmasks before and after; flags the curve already has are a success with applied=false, saved=false and a note, and nothing is written or saved; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. get_anim_curve_data reads the flags.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UAnimSequence |
| `curve_name` | string | yes | Name of the curve |
| `interp_mode` | string | yes | One of "linear\|editable\|metadata\|drive_track\|disabled" |
| `curve_type` | string | no | Curve type to target: float (default) or transform |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, curve_name, interp_mode, old_flags, new_flags, applied, saved, save_error, note? }`

## `set_anim_curve_keys`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Replace every key of an existing float curve on a UAnimSequence with the given [time, value] pairs as linear keys with auto tangents, through its data controller in an undo transaction, then save the package; num_keys is read back. The curve must exist (add_anim_float_curve first) and keys needs at least one valid pair. A transform curve is refused, since its keys are transforms, not [time, value] pairs: rekey it with add_anim_transform_curve. Any other curve_type is an error, and so is a rekey the data controller rejects, with nothing saved. A curve that already holds exactly those keys is a success with applied=false, saved=false and a note, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UAnimSequence |
| `curve_name` | string | yes | Name of the float curve (e.g. "MyCurve") |
| `keys` | array | no | JSON array of [time, value] pairs, time in seconds, at least one; entries that are not such a pair are skipped, and tangents or interpolation cannot be given. |
| `curve_type` | string | no | Curve type to target: float (default) or transform; transform is refused with an error pointing at add_anim_transform_curve. |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, curve_name, curve_type, num_keys, applied, saved, save_error, note? }`

## `set_anim_frame_rate`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the frame rate of the data model of a UAnimSequence (IAnimationDataController::SetFrameRate, one undo step) to fps rounded to whole frames per second, then save the package; fps, numerator and denominator are read back from the data model. The data controller only takes a rate that is a multiple or a factor of the current one, and the frame count must stay whole at the new rate: any other rate is an error and nothing changes. The rate the data model already has is a success with changed=false, saved=false and a note, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. get_anim_sequence_info reads the rate.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `fps` | number | yes | New frame rate in frames per second, rounded to a whole number that must be at least 1. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path, fps, numerator, denominator, changed, saved, save_error, note? }`

## `set_anim_graph_node_pin_binding`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Bind an AnimGraph node input pin to a variable or property path in the node property-binding map (the Details-panel bind chip), e.g. "TransformTrajectory" to "Trajectory"; set_anim_graph_node_property edits the FAnimNode struct instead. Returns applied and the stored binding; saves the AnimBP without recompiling (run compile_anim_blueprint).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the target UAnimGraphNode_* (from get_graph_nodes). |
| `pin_name` | string | yes | The bound property/pin name (e.g. "TransformTrajectory"). |
| `binding_path` | string | yes | The variable/property path to bind the pin to (e.g. "Trajectory", or nested "MyStruct.Member"). This tool does not check that the path resolves. |
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | no | Path or name of the UAnimBlueprint (aliases: anim_blueprint, blueprint_name). |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph (optional; deep-resolved; default the top-level AnimGraph). |
| `anim_blueprint` | string | no | Alias of anim_blueprint_path, used only when anim_blueprint_path is absent or empty. |
| `blueprint_name` | string | no | Alias of anim_blueprint_path, used only when anim_blueprint_path and anim_blueprint are both absent or empty. |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, pin_name, binding_path, applied, binding:{property_name, property_path[], path_as_text, is_bound, is_promotion, binding_type, pin_category}, saved }`

## `set_anim_graph_node_property`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Write a property of an AnimGraphNode's internal FAnimNode struct by (dotted) name. Saves the ABP but does NOT recompile it -- run compile_anim_blueprint after your edits for runtime effect.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Path/name of the UAnimBlueprint. |
| `node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the target AnimGraphNode. |
| `property` | string | yes | Property path inside the FAnimNode (e.g. "PoseCount", "SlotName"). A leading "Node." is tolerated. Nested structs use dots ("A.B"). |
| `value` | string | no | Text value (UE ImportText form: number, "EnumName", "(X=1,Y=2)"...). Use for scalars/enums/simple structs. |
| `value_json` | any | no | JSON value applied via JsonValueToUProperty. Use for complex/nested types. Takes precedence over value. |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph (optional, default the top-level AnimGraph). |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, property, applied, new_value, saved }`

## `set_anim_montage_preview_mesh`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the editor preview USkeletalMesh of a UAnimMontage (SetPreviewMesh, one undo step) and save the montage; it only changes what the asset editor shows, and the mesh skeleton is not checked against the montage. Returns mesh_path, prev_mesh_path and applied; the preview mesh the montage already has is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and the montage is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'). |
| `mesh_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the preview USkeletalMesh (e.g. '/Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube'). |

**Returns:** `{ montage_path, mesh_path, prev_mesh_path, applied, saved, save_error, message }`

## `set_anim_montage_rate_scale`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the global RateScale (and optionally BlendOutTriggerTime) on a UAnimMontage in an undo transaction and save it. Values the montage already has, or none given, are a success with applied=false and saved=false, and the montage is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Path to the UAnimMontage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'). |
| `name` | string | no | Alias of montage_path |
| `rate_scale` | number | no | Global play rate scale (defaults to current value) |
| `blend_out_trigger_time` | number | no | Blend-out trigger time in seconds (defaults to current value) |

**Returns:** `{ montage_path, rate_scale, blend_out_trigger_time, applied, saved, save_error, message }`

## `set_anim_montage_skeleton`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Rebind a UAnimMontage to a different USkeleton (clears existing source link + recomputes bone caches) in an undo transaction and save it. The skeleton the montage already uses is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and the montage is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'). |

## `set_anim_number_of_frames`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the number of frames of the data model of a UAnimSequence (IAnimationDataController::SetNumberOfFrames, one undo step), then save the package; frame_count is read back from the data model. When the data model rate differs from the sequence sampling rate (as after set_anim_frame_rate), a count that is not a whole number of frames at the sampling rate is an error naming the multiple to use, with nothing changed. Each per-platform override of the sampling rate that the engine compresses at (a valid rate other than the default that is a multiple or a factor of it) is checked the same way, and the error names the platform; an override with a non-positive numerator is an error too. The current count gives saved=false and a note, with nothing saved. A count the data controller rejects is an error with nothing saved, and a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `frame_count` | number | yes | New number of frames (integer > 0). |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path, frame_count, saved, save_error, note? }`

## `set_anim_retarget_source`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set a UAnimSequence's retarget source (and optionally its retarget reference-pose sequence) in an undo transaction and save it. A ref_pose_seq_path that does not load is an error before anything changes; values the sequence already has are a success with changed=false, applied_count 0, saved=false and a note, and nothing is modified or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Object path of the UAnimSequence to mutate. |
| `retarget_source` | string | no | Retarget-source name (FName). Must name an entry in the owning skeleton's retarget-source map to RESOLVE at runtime, but the property write persists regardless. Use 'None' (or empty) to clear. |
| `ref_pose_seq_path` | string | no | Optional object path of a UAnimSequence used as the additive retarget reference pose (RefPoseSeq). Pass empty/'None' to clear it. |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, retarget_source, ref_pose_seq, ref_pose_seq_set, ref_pose_seq_cleared, applied_count, notes, changed, success, saved, save_error, note? }`

## `set_anim_root_motion`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Write the three root motion settings of a UAnimSequence (bEnableRootMotion, RootMotionRootLock, bForceRootLock) and save it. All three are written on every call, so an omitted one is reset to its default; an unknown root lock name applies RefPose while the reply echoes the given text. Settings the sequence already has are a success with changed=false and saved=false, and the sequence is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `enable_root_motion` | boolean | no | Whether to enable root motion extraction (default true) |
| `root_motion_root_lock` | string | no | Root lock mode: RefPose\|AnimFirstFrame\|Zero (default RefPose) |
| `force_root_lock` | boolean | no | Whether to force the root lock (default false) |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, enable_root_motion, root_motion_root_lock, force_root_lock, changed, success, saved, save_error, message }`

## `set_anim_transition_rule_automatic`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the automatic rule of one transition (source_state to target_state) in a state machine of an Animation Blueprint: bAutomaticRuleBasedOnSequencePlayerInState and AutomaticRuleTriggerTime, both written every call (omitted means false and 0). Marks it structurally modified and saves without compiling; refused while PIE runs unless force=true.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |

| `machine_name` | string | yes | Name of the state machine that owns the transition |
| `source_state` | string | yes | Name of the source state (transition origin) |
| `target_state` | string | yes | Name of the target state (transition destination) |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | True lets the transition fire on its own when the sequence player of the source state nears its end (bAutomaticRuleBasedOnSequencePlayerInState); omitted writes false. |
| `trigger_time` | number | no | AutomaticRuleTriggerTime in seconds (default 0.0; negative = blend lead) |

**Returns:** `{ anim_blueprint_path, machine_name, source_state, target_state, enabled, trigger_time, rule_graph_has_result_node, saved, save_error? }`

## `set_animation_speed`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the play rate of a skeletal mesh component, found by object name in the editor world (or the world the world param selects), and switch its component tick on. Only a component in Use Animation Asset (single node) mode takes it: in Animation Blueprint mode nothing changes and actual_speed reads 0, so check speed_set_successfully. Transient: nothing is saved or undoable. A speed outside 0-10 or no such component is an error. For montages use play_animation with play_rate, or set_anim_montage_rate_scale on the asset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `component_name` | string | yes | Object name of the USkeletalMeshComponent, e.g. "CharacterMesh0", case-insensitive; the first actor in the world that has one with that name wins |
| `speed` | number | yes | Playback speed multiplier; must be between 0.0 and 10.0 |
| `world` | string | no | Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) \| 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) \| 'server' (the PIE world with authority) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' \| 'game' (alias of 'pie'). |

**Returns:** `{ component_name: string, requested_speed: number, previous_speed: number, actual_speed: number, speed_set_successfully: bool, previous_tick_enabled: bool, current_tick_enabled: bool, component_valid: bool, component_class: string, anim_instance_class: string?, has_anim_instance: bool, anim_instance_valid: bool?, warning: string?, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }`

## `set_blendspace_interpolation`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set a blend space's INPUT-SMOOTHING (interpolation) per axis: smoothing time, damping ratio, max speed, smoothing type.  Distinct from set_blendspace_properties (which only sets the BlendParameters axis name/min/max/grid). Writes UBlendSpace::InterpolationParam[axis] via reflection. 1D smooths axis 0 only; 2D smooths X (axis 0) and Y (axis 1). Only the supplied fields change, in one undo transaction, then the blend space is saved; an unknown smoothing type is an error before anything changes, and values the axes already have are a success with changed=false, applied_count 0, saved=false and a note, with nothing modified or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blend_space_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the UBlendSpace / UBlendSpace1D. |
| `x_interpolation_time` | number | no | Optional X-axis smoothing time in seconds (>= 0; 0 disables smoothing). |
| `x_damping_ratio` | number | no | Optional X-axis damping ratio (>= 0; only used when type is SpringDamper). |
| `x_max_speed` | number | no | Optional X-axis maximum speed in real units (>= 0; only used when type is SpringDamper or Exponential). |
| `x_interpolation_type` | string | no | Optional X-axis smoothing type: Averaged\|Linear\|Cubic\|EaseInOut\|Exponential\|SpringDamper. |
| `y_interpolation_time` | number | no | Optional Y-axis smoothing time in seconds (2D only, >= 0). |
| `y_damping_ratio` | number | no | Optional Y-axis damping ratio (2D only, >= 0). |
| `y_max_speed` | number | no | Optional Y-axis maximum speed (2D only, >= 0). |
| `y_interpolation_type` | string | no | Optional Y-axis smoothing type (2D only): Averaged\|Linear\|Cubic\|EaseInOut\|Exponential\|SpringDamper. |

**Returns:** `{ blend_space_path, is_1d, x_axis: {interpolation_time, damping_ratio, max_speed, interpolation_type}, y_axis: {...}, applied_count, notes, changed, saved, save_error, note? }`

| `y_axis_name` | string | no | Optional Y axis display name (2D only). |
| `y_axis_min` | number | no | Optional Y axis minimum value (2D only). |
| `y_axis_max` | number | no | Optional Y axis maximum value (2D only). |
| `y_axis_grid` | integer | no | Optional Y axis grid divisions (2D only, >= 1). |

**Returns:** `{ blend_space_path, is_1d, x_axis: {name, min, max, grid}, y_axis: {name, min, max, grid}, applied_count, notes, changed, saved, save_error, note? }`

## `set_ik_bone_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set bone-specific settings for a bone within a solver, as one undo transaction, then save the IK Rig asset; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.  Partial update (idempotent): only fields present in ``settings`` are applied; bone settings are auto-created if absent (a bone the rig skeleton lacks is an error, with nothing changed), and existing settings that already have those values give changed false, saved false and a note, with nothing saved. FullBodyIK snake_case keys: rotation_stiffness (0-1), position_stiffness (0-1), limit_x/limit_y/limit_z ("Free"/"Limited"/"Locked"), min_x, max_x, min_y, max_y, min_z, max_z, use_preferred_angles (bool), preferred_x, preferred_y, preferred_z. StretchLimb uses its live bone struct's camelCase keys (squashDirection: {x,y,z}). Only FullBodyIK and StretchLimb support per-bone settings; others return an honest error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Content path to the IK Rig asset. |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | Index of the solver. |
| `bone_name` | string | yes | Name of the bone to modify. |
| `settings` | object | yes | Object with bone-specific fields to set. |

**Returns:** `{ ik_rig_path: string, solver_index: int, bone_name: string, success: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `set_ik_goal_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set goal-specific settings for a goal connected to a solver, as one undo transaction, then save the IK Rig asset.  Partial update (idempotent): only fields present in ``settings`` are applied. FullBodyIK uses snake_case keys: bone_name, chain_depth (0+), strength_alpha (0-1), pull_chain_alpha (0-1), pin_rotation (0-1). BodyMover uses its live goal struct's camelCase keys (influenceMultiplier 0-10, clamped server-side). Connect the goal first with connect_ik_goal_to_solver. Solvers without per-goal settings return an honest error. Settings that already have those values give changed false, saved false and a note, with nothing saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Content path to the IK Rig asset. |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | Index of the solver. |
| `goal_name` | string | yes | Name of the goal to modify. |
| `settings` | object | yes | Object with goal-specific fields to set. |

**Returns:** `{ ik_rig_path: string, solver_index: int, goal_name: string, success: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `set_ik_retarget_chain_bones`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Change the start bone, end bone and/or IK goal of an existing retarget chain in an IK Rig asset through the IK Rig controller (each change an undo transaction), then save the asset. Pass at least one of the three, else an error. A missing chain, a bone not in the rig skeleton or a goal_name the rig has no goal for is not an error but start_bone_set, end_bone_set or goal_set false, and that field is left unchanged. A value the chain already has is left alone; when nothing changes, changed is false, saved is false, a note says why and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Siblings: add_ik_retarget_chain, rename_ik_retarget_chain.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset |
| `chain_name` | string | yes | Name of the retarget chain to mutate |
| `start_bone` | string | no | Optional new start bone |
| `end_bone` | string | no | Optional new end bone |
| `goal_name` | string | no | Optional new associated IK goal, which must be a goal of the rig; None clears the goal of the chain. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, chain_name: string, start_bone: string, end_bone: string, goal_name: string, start_bone_set: bool, end_bone_set: bool, goal_set: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `set_ik_solver_bones`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the start bone and/or end bone of one solver in an IK Rig asset (0-based stack index) through the IK Rig controller, which records each change as an undo transaction, then save the asset. Pass at least one bone, else an error. An out-of-range index, a bone missing from the rig skeleton, or a start or end bone on a solver type without one is not an error: start_bone_set or end_bone_set comes back false, next to the bones read back, and nothing is stored for it. A bone the solver already has is left alone; when nothing changes, changed is false, saved is false, a note says why and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. get_ik_solver_bones reads them.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | 0-based solver index |
| `start_bone` | string | no | Optional start bone name |
| `end_bone` | string | no | Optional end bone name |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, solver_index: int, start_bone: string, end_bone: string, start_bone_set: bool, end_bone_set: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `set_ik_solver_enabled`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Enable or disable the solver at a 0-based index of an IK Rig asset through the IK Rig controller (one undo transaction), then save the asset; enabled is read back. An out-of-range index is not an error but set_ok false, and a solver already in the requested state gives changed false: in both cases saved is false, a note says why and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | 0-based solver index |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Optional bool; defaults to true |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, solver_index: int, enabled: bool, set_ok: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `set_ik_solver_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set detailed solver-specific settings on a solver in an IK Rig, as one undo transaction, then save the asset.  Partial update: only fields present in ``settings`` are applied (idempotent). FullBodyIK uses snake_case keys: root_bone, iterations (0-1000), sub_iterations (0-1000), mass_multiplier (0-10), allow_stretch (bool), root_behavior (enum string), global_pull_chain_alpha (0-1), max_angle (0-45), over_relaxation (1-2). Other solver types (Limb/Pole/BodyMover/SetTransform/StretchLimb) accept the camelCase names of their live settings struct; ClampMin/ClampMax bounds are enforced server-side. Settings that already have those values give changed false, saved false and a note, with nothing saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Content path to the IK Rig asset. |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | Index of the solver in the rig's solver stack. |
| `settings` | object | yes | Object with solver-type-specific fields to set. |

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the AnimStartTime on an existing FAnimSegment by (slot_name, segment_index), clamped to [0, AnimEndTime], in an undo transaction, and save the montage. AnimEndTime is left untouched. The (clamped) start time the segment already has is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and the montage is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'). |
| `slot_name` | string | yes | Name of the slot track containing the segment. |
| `segment_index` | number | yes | Zero-based index into the slot track's AnimSegments. |
| `start_time` | number | yes | New AnimStartTime in seconds (clamped to [0, AnimEndTime]). |

**Returns:** `{ montage_path, slot_name, segment_index, start_time, anim_end_time, applied, saved, save_error, message, note? }`

## `set_morph_target_deltas`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set vertex deltas for a morph target on a specific LOD.  Each delta is a dict with keys: vertex_index (int), position_delta ({x,y,z}), normal_delta ({x,y,z}).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset |
| `morph_target_name` | string | yes | Name of the morph target to modify |
| `deltas` | array | yes | List of delta dicts, e.g. [{"vertex_index": 0, "position_delta": {"x": 1.0, "y": 0, "z": 0}, "normal_delta": {"x": 0, "y": 0, "z": 0}}] |
| `lod_index` | number | no | LOD index to populate (default 0) |

**Returns:** `{ morph_target_name: string, lod_index: int, deltas_set: int, total_deltas_lod0: int, saved: bool }`

## `set_morph_target_generated_by_engine`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Flag morph targets of a skeletal mesh asset as generated by engine tools rather than imported from a source file, on every LOD, then save the mesh (a failed save is an error). The flag is only ever set, never cleared; names not on the mesh are ignored, and an empty or missing list flags every morph. When any flag changes the engine runs PreEditChange/PostEditChange on the mesh, which rebuilds it. modified says whether anything changed; flagged lists every morph now marked on LOD 0. Names come from get_skeletal_mesh_morph_targets.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset |
| `morph_target_names` | array | no | List of morph target names to flag; empty list = flag every morph on the mesh |

**Returns:** `{ skeletal_mesh_path: string, requested_count: int, named_list: bool, modified: bool, flagged: [string], note: string }`

## `set_motion_warping_component_search_in_anims`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set bSearchForWindowsInAnimsWithinMontages on the UMotionWarpingComponent of an editor-world actor found by internal name (not label): when true, warping windows are also searched in animations inside montages. Marks the level dirty, not saved; returns previous and new values and changed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Internal object name of the actor with the UMotionWarpingComponent, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_0"; the outliner label does not match. |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Sets bSearchForWindowsInAnimsWithinMontages: when true, motion-warping windows are also searched in animations nested inside montages (required, no default) |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name, previous_search_in_anims: bool, new_search_in_anims: bool, changed: bool }`

## `set_motion_warping_target_bone_name`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the BoneName on an existing FMotionWarpingTarget (resolves the existing Component ref).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Engine name of the actor carrying the UMotionWarpingComponent |
| `warp_target_name` | string | yes | FName of the existing warp target on the component |
| `bone_name` | string | yes | Skeletal bone on the target's Component to anchor to; NAME_None follows the component root |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name, warp_target_name, previous_bone_name: string, new_bone_name: string, changed: bool }`

## `set_motion_warping_target_follow_component`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set bFollowComponent on an existing component-based warp target of an editor-world actor found by internal name, keeping its Component, BoneName and offsets. A missing target, or one without a Component, is an error. WarpTargets is Transient, so the change is not saved with the level.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Internal object name of the actor with the UMotionWarpingComponent, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_0"; the outliner label does not match. |
| `warp_target_name` | string | yes | FName of the existing warp target on the component |
| `follow` | boolean | yes | When true the target tracks the Component's live transform each frame; when false it snapshots the current transform (required, no default) |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name, warp_target_name, previous_follow: bool, new_follow: bool, changed: bool }`

## `set_motion_warping_target_location`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Update an existing FMotionWarpingTarget's location (and optionally rotation) by FName -- an idempotent replace-in-place. Choose this over add_warp_target_to_component when the target already exists and you only want to nudge where it points; add_warp_target_to_component is the one that CREATES a target.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Engine name of the actor carrying the UMotionWarpingComponent |
| `warp_target_name` | string | yes | FName of the existing target |
| `location` | array | no | [x, y, z] world location |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] rotation; defaults to ZeroRotator |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name, warp_target_name, location_set, previous_count, new_count }`

## `set_motion_warping_target_location_offset`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set LocationOffset (FVector) on an existing FMotionWarpingTarget (keeps BoneName/follow/rotation-offset).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Engine name of the actor carrying the UMotionWarpingComponent |
| `warp_target_name` | string | yes | FName of the existing warp target on the component |
| `location_offset` | array | no | [x, y, z] offset applied to the target relative to its LocationOffsetDirection |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name, warp_target_name, previous_x, previous_y, previous_z, new_x, new_y, new_z, changed: bool }`

## `set_motion_warping_target_rotation`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the rotation of an existing warp target of an editor-world actor (found by internal name), keeping its Location. The target is rebuilt as a plain transform target, so a component-based one loses its Component, BoneName, follow flag and offsets. WarpTargets is Transient: not saved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Internal object name of the actor with the UMotionWarpingComponent, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_0"; the outliner label does not match. |
| `warp_target_name` | string | yes | FName of the existing warp target on the component |
| `rotation` | array | no | New world rotation in degrees as [pitch, yaw, roll]; omitted means [0, 0, 0]. |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name, warp_target_name, previous_pitch, previous_yaw, previous_roll, new_pitch, new_yaw, new_roll, changed: bool }`

## `set_pose_asset_base_pose`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set which named pose of a UPoseAsset is its base pose (UPoseAsset::SetBasePoseName) in an undo transaction, then save the asset; an empty or None base_pose_name goes back to the skeleton reference pose. A name the asset does not contain is an error before anything changes, and so is a base pose the engine does not take (read back from the asset), with nothing saved. The base pose the asset already has is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and nothing is modified or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. The base pose only drives evaluation of an additive pose asset, which additive and note report. Edit poses with add_pose_to_pose_asset, rename_pose_in_pose_asset and remove_pose_from_pose_asset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pose_asset_path` | string | yes | Path to the UPoseAsset. |
| `base_pose_name` | string | no | Name of the pose to use as the base; empty/None resets to the reference pose. |

**Returns:** `{ pose_asset_path, base_pose_name, requested_name, applied, base_pose_index, is_reference_pose, additive, note, saved, save_error, message }`

## `set_pose_search_database_schema`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Bind a UPoseSearchSchema to a UPoseSearchDatabase (assigns the Schema field). Use it right after creating a database with no schema, or to rebind an existing one; a database without a schema cannot be indexed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `database_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UPoseSearchDatabase (required). |
| `schema_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UPoseSearchSchema to bind (required). |

**Returns:** `{ database_path, previous_schema_path, new_schema_path, changed: bool, saved: bool }`

## `set_pose_search_schema_mirror_data_table`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Bind (or rebind) the UMirrorDataTable of the schema's FPoseSearchRoledSkeleton entry under `role` (default role when omitted). Refused when no entry has that role.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UPoseSearchSchema to edit (required). |
| `mirror_data_table_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UMirrorDataTable to bind under the given role (required). |
| `role` | string | no | Role name (FName) identifying the FPoseSearchRoledSkeleton entry within a multi-character schema (optional; empty = default role). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, role, previous_mirror_data_table_path, new_mirror_data_table_path, changed, saved }`

## `set_pose_search_schema_properties`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Author UPoseSearchSchema scalar tunables via reflection (partial merge + clamp). Replaces the 8 former per-field set_pose_search_schema_* setters.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the target UPoseSearchSchema (required). |
| `properties` | object | yes | Object of UPoseSearchSchema UPROPERTY fields to merge; keys are the C++ property NAMES (case-insensitive), absent keys untouched. Covers: SampleRate(int, ClampMin=1 ClampMax=240), bAddDataPadding(bool), bInjectAdditionalDebugChannels(bool), bDrawInjectAdditionalDebugChannels(bool), NumberOfPermutations(int, ClampMin=1), PermutationsSampleRate(int, ClampMin=1 ClampMax=240), PermutationsTimeOffset(float), DataPreprocessor(enum name: None/Normalize/NormalizeOnlyByDeviation/NormalizeWithCommonSchema). Object-refs (skeleton, mirror_data_table) and the role tag are set via their dedicated commands, not here. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, asset_class, settings, applied_keys, changed, saved }`

## `set_pose_search_schema_role`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Rename the role (FName) of the schema's FPoseSearchRoledSkeleton entry under role_from (default role when omitted). Refused when new_role is already taken by another entry.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UPoseSearchSchema to edit (required). |
| `new_role` | string | yes | New role name (FName) to assign to the entry, identifying it within a multi-character schema (required). |
| `role_from` | string | no | Existing role name (FName) of the FPoseSearchRoledSkeleton entry to rename (optional; empty = default role). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, previous_role, new_role, changed, saved }`

## `set_pose_search_schema_skeleton`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Bind (or rebind) the USkeleton of the schema's FPoseSearchRoledSkeleton entry under `role`. Idempotent by role: if a skeleton is already bound under that role it is REPLACED; if no roled entry exists for that role yet, one is created. Use add_pose_search_roled_skeleton instead when you want to ADD a second character's role without disturbing the first.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UPoseSearchSchema to edit (required). |
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the USkeleton to bind under the given role (required). |
| `role` | string | no | Role name (FName) identifying the FPoseSearchRoledSkeleton entry within a multi-character schema (optional; empty = default role). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, role, previous_skeleton_path, new_skeleton_path, changed, saved }`

## `set_retarget_pose_bone_rotation`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set a bone's rotation offset in the current retarget pose (euler degrees) of an IK Retargeter asset, as one undo transaction, then save the asset; the offset is read back as quat_x..quat_w. Creates a default pose if none is current. bone_name is stored as given, not checked against the skeleton. When the pose to edit is already current and already holds exactly that offset for the bone, changed is false, saved is false, a note says so and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_retargeter_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRetargeter asset |
| `bone_name` | string | yes | Name of the bone to update |
| `source_or_target` | string | no | Optional "Source" or "Target" scope; defaults to "Target" |
| `pitch` | number | no | Euler pitch in degrees (used when no quat is provided) |
| `yaw` | number | no | Euler yaw in degrees |
| `roll` | number | no | Euler roll in degrees |
| `quat_x` | number | no | Optional quaternion X |
| `quat_y` | number | no | Optional quaternion Y |
| `quat_z` | number | no | Optional quaternion Z |
| `quat_w` | number | no | Optional quaternion W |
| `rotation` | object | no | Optional nested {x, y, z, w} quaternion object |
| `pose_name` | string | no | Optional explicit retarget pose name; created if missing |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, bone_name: string, source_or_target: string, retarget_pose: string, quat_x: number, quat_y: number, quat_z: number, quat_w: number, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `set_retargeter_chain_mapping`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Make source_chain drive target_chain in an IK Retargeter asset, overwriting the previous mapping, on every op whose chain mapping lists target_chain (or only the op named op_name), in one undo transaction, then save the asset. source_chain is not validated, so a misspelled name is stored as given. set_ok is false when no op lists target_chain; mapped_source is read back from the first matching op. When no op lists target_chain, or every one already maps it to source_chain, changed is false, saved is false, a note says why and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. get_ik_retargeter_info shows the per-op mappings.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_retargeter_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRetargeter asset |
| `source_chain` | string | yes | Name of the source retarget chain |
| `target_chain` | string | yes | Name of the target retarget chain to map to |
| `op_name` | string | no | Optional op name as get_ik_retargeter_info lists it; omitted, every op whose chain mapping lists target_chain is updated |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, source_chain: string, target_chain: string, mapped_source: string, set_ok: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `set_retargeter_op_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Partial-merge a retarget op's live settings struct (only the JSON fields present are written -> idempotent), and optionally toggle the op enabled flag, as one undo transaction, then save the asset.  Settings keys match get_retargeter_op_info (first char lower-cased, e.g. lODThreshold). Numeric ClampMin/ClampMax metadata is enforced after the merge. The optional `enabled` flag is applied via the controller. The payload echoes the read-back settings. When neither is given, or the op already has those settings and that enabled state, changed is false, saved is false, a note says why and nothing is saved. An out-of-range op_index is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_retargeter_path` | string | yes | Content path to the UIKRetargeter asset. |
| `op_index` | number | yes | 0-based index of the op in the retargeter's op stack. |
| `settings` | object | no | Partial settings object; only present fields are written (e.g. { lODThreshold: 5 }). |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Optional: enable/disable the op (applied via the controller). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, op_index: int, op_name: string, op_type: string, enabled: bool, settings: object, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `set_rig_control_limits`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set a scalar Control Rig control's min/max limits (Float/ScaleFloat/Integer).  Enables the limit array for the control type and sets MinimumValue/MaximumValue type-correctly; once enabled, set_rig_control_value clamps via ApplyLimits. Verified read-back.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UControlRigBlueprint asset. |
| `control_name` | string | yes | Name of an existing control element (Float/ScaleFloat/Integer). |
| `min` | number | yes | Minimum value (number). |
| `max` | number | yes | Maximum value (number). |
| `enable` | boolean | no | Whether to enable the limits (optional, default true). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, control_name: string, control_type: string, min: number, max: number, limit_enabled: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_rig_control_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Edit an existing Control Rig control's shape/gizmo/color/limit-draw settings (the bits add_rig_control can't set afterwards).  Read-modify-write: reads the control's FRigControlSettings, applies the provided fields, writes back via URigHierarchyController::SetControlSettings, recompiles + saves, and returns the verified read-back. Only the supplied fields change.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UControlRigBlueprint asset. |
| `control_name` | string | yes | Name of an existing control element. |
| `display_name` | string | no | Optional display name (FName) for the control. |
| `shape_name` | string | no | Optional gizmo shape name (e.g. "Default", "Box", "Sphere", "Circle"). |
| `shape_color` | array | no | Optional shape color [R, G, B] or [R, G, B, A] floats (0..1). |
| `shape_visible` | boolean | no | Optional bool: whether the gizmo shape is visible in 3D. |
| `draw_limits` | boolean | no | Optional bool: whether to draw the control's limits in debug. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, control_name: string, settings_applied: { display_name, shape_name, shape_color: [float], shape_visible, draw_limits }, applied_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_rig_control_shape_transform`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the local shape (gizmo) transform of an existing Control Rig control.  Reads the current local shape transform, overrides only the supplied location/rotation/scale, writes back via URigHierarchy::SetControlShapeTransform, recompiles + saves, and returns the verified read-back. This positions the manipulator gizmo relative to the control, independent of the control's value.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UControlRigBlueprint asset. |
| `control_name` | string | yes | Name of an existing control element. |
| `location` | array | no | Optional [X, Y, Z] gizmo location. |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional [Pitch, Yaw, Roll] gizmo rotation. |
| `scale` | array | no | Optional [X, Y, Z] gizmo scale. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, control_name: string, shape_transform: { location: [float], rotation: [float], scale: [float] }, applied_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_rig_control_value`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set a Control Rig control's pose value (Initial + Current), type-correct per the control's ERigControlType.  add_rig_control only seeds the identity value. SetControlValue applies the control's limits, so a value outside an enabled min/max is clamped (set limits first with set_rig_control_limits). Verified read-back.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UControlRigBlueprint asset. |
| `control_name` | string | yes | Name of an existing control element. |
| `value` | string | no | The value: bool (Bool), number (Float/ScaleFloat/Integer), or [x,y(,z)] (Vector2D/Position/Scale/Rotator). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, control_name: string, control_type: string, value: any, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_rigvm_pin_default`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the default value of a pin in the main RigVM graph of a Control Rig Blueprint (URigVMController::SetPinDefaultValue, no undo entry), then compile and save it. success reflects the save even when the write failed: check set, pin_found and current_value, which is read back.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control_rig_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UControlRigBlueprint, e.g. "/Game/Rigs/CR_Mannequin". |
| `pin_path` | string | yes | Pin path NodeName.PinName, e.g. SetTransform.bInitial |
| `value` | string | yes | Value in UE export-text form, e.g. "true", "1.0" or "(X=0.0,Y=0.0,Z=1.0)"; array pins are resized to the given element count. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, pin_path: string, value: string, set: bool, pin_found: bool, current_value: string, saved: bool, save_error: string }`

## `set_skeletal_mesh_allow_cpu_access`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set bAllowCPUAccess on every LOD of a skeletal mesh. Used to keep vertex/skin data resident for FX sampling or other CPU work.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset |
| `b_allow` | boolean | no | New value for the flag (default true) |

**Returns:** `{ skeletal_mesh_path: string, b_allow: bool, applied_lods: int, saved: bool }`

## `set_skeletal_mesh_anim_class`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Repoint a Blueprint's skeletal mesh component AnimClass to a (fork) AnimBlueprint. Also handles the INHERITED native Character Mesh, which is not in the SCS and which the generic component-property setters cannot reach: it writes the CDO component archetype so spawned instances inherit the new AnimClass. Also sets AnimationMode=AnimationBlueprint.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Character/Actor Blueprint (name or path), e.g. "BP_MyCharacter". |
| `anim_class` | string | yes | The AnimBlueprint to use: an ABP asset path (resolved to its generated class) or a "..._C" class path/name. |
| `component_name` | string | no | Skeletal mesh component to target (optional). Omit to target the Character's inherited Mesh. |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint, component, anim_class, previous_anim_class, applied, wrote_cdo_archetype, saved }`

## `set_skeletal_mesh_lod_build_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Change the stored build settings of one LOD of a skeletal mesh asset, only the fields you pass, and save the mesh. The mesh is not rebuilt here, so the settings take effect at its next build or reimport; a failed save returns an error. Returns settings_applied.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Skeletal mesh asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero". |
| `lod_index` | number | no | 0-based LOD index (default 0); an index the mesh does not have fails the call. |
| `recompute_normals` | boolean | no | Ignore the imported normals and recompute them (bRecomputeNormals). |
| `recompute_tangents` | boolean | no | Ignore the imported tangents and recompute them (bRecomputeTangents). |
| `use_mikk_t_space` | boolean | no | Use MikkTSpace when computing tangents (bUseMikkTSpace). |
| `compute_weighted_normals` | boolean | no | Weight computed normals by triangle area and corner angle (bComputeWeightedNormals). |
| `remove_degenerates` | boolean | no | Remove degenerate triangles at build time (bRemoveDegenerates). |
| `high_precision_tangents` | boolean | no | Store tangents at 16-bit instead of 8-bit precision (bUseHighPrecisionTangentBasis). |
| `high_precision_weights` | boolean | no | Use 16-bit instead of 8-bit skin weights for rendering (bUseHighPrecisionSkinWeights). |
| `full_precision_uvs` | boolean | no | Store UVs at full floating-point precision (bUseFullPrecisionUVs). |
| `bone_influence_limit` | number | no | Maximum bone influences per vertex; 0 uses the DefaultBoneInfluenceLimit project setting, and values above the project limit have no effect. |

**Returns:** `{ lod_index: int, settings_applied: {...}, saved: bool }`

## `set_skeletal_mesh_lod_reduction_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Author a LOD's FSkeletalMeshOptimizationSettings (ReductionSettings) — the data bake_skeletal_mesh_lod consumes, making the bake steerable instead of running with defaults.  Partial update (idempotent): only fields present are written. Enums are by name (full "SMTC_NumOfTriangles" or short "NumOfTriangles"). termination_criterion (SMTC_*) and reduction_method (SMOT_*) are DISTINCT.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset. |
| `lod_index` | number | no | LOD index to modify (default 0). |
| `termination_criterion` | string | no | SMTC_*: NumOfTriangles\|NumOfVerts\|TriangleOrVert\|AbsNumOfTriangles\|AbsNumOfVerts\|AbsTriangleOrVert. |
| `reduction_method` | string | no | SMOT_*: NumOfTriangles\|MaxDeviation\|TriangleOrDeviation. |
| `num_of_triangles_percentage` | number | no | float ratio of triangles to retain (0.1 = 10%). |
| `num_of_vert_percentage` | number | no | float ratio of vertices to retain. |
| `max_deviation_percentage` | number | no | float [0,1], accuracy target when reduction_method=MaxDeviation. |
| `max_num_of_triangles` | number | no | int absolute triangle cap (ClampMin 4). |
| `max_num_of_verts` | number | no | int absolute vertex cap (ClampMin 6). |
| `max_num_of_triangles_percentage` | number | no | int (editor-only) cap when using percentage criterion (ClampMin 4). |
| `max_num_of_verts_percentage` | number | no | int (editor-only) cap when using percentage criterion (ClampMin 6). |
| `base_lod` | number | no | int base LOD index to generate from (default 0). |
| `silhouette_importance` | string | no | SMOI_*: Off\|Lowest\|Low\|Normal\|High\|Highest. |
| `texture_importance` | string | no | SMOI_* importance of texture density. |
| `shading_importance` | string | no | SMOI_* importance of shading quality. |
| `skinning_importance` | string | no | SMOI_* importance of skinning quality. |
| `max_bones_per_vertex` | number | no | int max bone influences per vertex (ClampMin 1). |
| `welding_threshold` | number | no | float vertex weld distance. |
| `normals_threshold` | number | no | float hard-edge angle in degrees (used when recalc_normals). |
| `recalc_normals` | boolean | no | bool recompute normals. |
| `remap_morph_targets` | boolean | no | bool remap morph targets onto the reduced LOD. |
| `enforce_bone_boundaries` | boolean | no | bool penalize collapses across different major bones. |

**Returns:** `{ lod_index: int, settings_applied: {...}, saved: bool }`

## `set_skeletal_mesh_lod_screen_size`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set ScreenSize.Default (the screen size at which this LOD switches in) of one LOD of a skeletal mesh asset. Marks the mesh dirty but does NOT save it, so follow with save_asset; per-platform overrides are left as they are. Returns old_screen_size and screen_size.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Skeletal mesh asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero". |
| `lod_index` | number | yes | 0-based LOD index; must be below the LOD count of the mesh. |
| `screen_size` | number | yes | New ScreenSize.Default value, e.g. 0.3; the call fails without it. |

**Returns:** `{ skeletal_mesh_path: string, lod_index: int, old_screen_size: float, screen_size: float, applied: bool }`

## `set_skeletal_mesh_lod_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the remaining flat per-LOD scalars/enums of FSkeletalMeshLODInfo that no other setter covers (hysteresis, CPU access, morph error tolerance, skin cache usage, mesh deformer, prioritization weight).  Partial update (idempotent): only fields present are written.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset. |
| `lod_index` | number | no | LOD index to modify (default 0). |
| `lod_hysteresis` | number | no | float, avoids flickering at the LOD boundary. |
| `allow_cpu_access` | boolean | no | bool, keep this LOD's data on the CPU (e.g. for FX sampling). |
| `morph_target_position_error_tolerance` | number | no | float in microns, Clamp 0.01..10000 (default 20). |
| `skin_cache_usage` | string | no | ESkinCacheUsage by NAME: Auto\|Disabled\|Enabled (Disabled=255, parsed by name). |
| `allow_mesh_deformer` | boolean | no | bool, whether a Mesh Deformer is used on this LOD. |
| `weight_of_prioritization` | number | no | float >=0, weight given to BonesToPrioritize/SectionsToPrioritize. |

**Returns:** `{ lod_index: int, settings_applied: {...}, saved: bool }`

## `set_skeletal_mesh_material_slot`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Assign a material to an existing material slot of a skeletal mesh ASSET (writes FSkeletalMaterial.MaterialInterface in USkeletalMesh::GetMaterials()). Address the slot by slot_index OR slot_name (exactly one). Never auto-grows the slot array.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the USkeletalMesh asset. |
| `material_path` | string | yes | Content path to the UMaterialInterface to assign. |
| `slot_index` | number | no | Zero-based index of an existing material slot (mutually exclusive with slot_name). |
| `slot_name` | string | no | Name of an existing material slot to resolve to its index (mutually exclusive with slot_index). |

**Returns:** `{ skeletal_mesh_path: string, slot_index: int, slot_name: string, material_path: string, saved: bool }`

## `set_skeletal_mesh_min_lod`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the platform-wide forced-min-LOD bias on a skeletal mesh.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset |
| `min_lod` | number | no | New MinLodIdx (must be in [0, NumLODs-1]) |

**Returns:** `{ skeletal_mesh_path: string, old_min_lod: int, min_lod: int, lod_count: int, applied: bool }`

## `set_skeletal_mesh_section_cast_shadow`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the cast shadow flag on a specific section of a skeletal mesh LOD.
